title: Poker Hand Evaluator
spec: The entry function `evaluate(hand)` receives a list of five tuples, where each tuple contains an integer value and a suit character. Determine the rank of the poker hand using explicit rules. Check if all suits are identical to identify a flush. Check if the values form a consecutive sequence to identify a straight. If both apply, it is a straight flush. Otherwise, group the values to count frequencies. Check if there are four identical values for a four of a kind. Check if there is a three of a kind and a pair for a full house. Check for a standalone three of a kind, two pairs, or a single pair. Return an integer from one to nine representing the hand strength, where nine is a straight flush and one is a high card.

title: Bowling Score Calculator
spec: The entry function `score(rolls)` receives a list of integers representing the number of pins knocked down in a bowling game. Iterate through the rolls using a loop to calculate the total score for exactly ten frames. Determine if a roll is a strike by checking if ten pins were knocked down in a single roll, which adds the next two rolls to the frame score. Otherwise, check if two consecutive rolls in a frame add up to ten to identify a spare, which adds the next single roll to the score. If neither a strike nor a spare occurs, simply add the two rolls of the frame. Check if the frame index reaches ten to stop processing regular frames and handle the bonus rolls correctly.

title: Markdown Parser
spec: The entry function `parse(lines)` takes a list of strings representing text lines and converts them into a list of html tags. Iterate through each line to check its starting characters. Determine if the line begins with one, two, or three hash symbols followed by a space to convert it into a header tag of the corresponding level. Check if the line starts with an asterisk to wrap it in list item tags. Check if the line starts with a greater than sign to format it as a blockquote. Check if the line is completely empty, and if so, skip it. For all other cases, wrap the plain text in paragraph tags.

title: ATM Withdrawal Simulator
spec: The entry function `withdraw(amount)` receives an integer representing the requested withdrawal amount. The machine holds one hundred, fifty, twenty, ten, five, and one dollar bills. Loop through these available denominations from largest to smallest. While the remaining amount is greater than or equal to the current denomination, subtract the denomination from the amount and increment a counter for that bill. Check if the requested amount is exactly zero at any point to stop the loop early. Check if the requested amount is negative or if it cannot be exactly dispensed, returning an empty list in those cases. Otherwise, return a list of six integers representing the count of each dispensed bill.

title: Vending Machine Coin Processor
spec: The entry function `vend(coins)` receives a list of integers representing inserted coin values in cents. The goal is to purchase an item costing seventy five cents. Loop through the coins and add them to a running total only if they are valid values of five, ten, or twenty five cents. If a coin is invalid, ignore it. Check if the total reaches or exceeds seventy five cents to stop accepting coins immediately. Once dispensing, check if change is required. Calculate how many quarters, dimes, and nickels to return by repeatedly checking if the change due is greater than or equal to the coin value and subtracting it. Return a tuple containing the purchased status as a boolean and a list of returned change coins.

title: Simplified Regex Matcher
spec: The entry function `match(pattern)` receives a string pattern and returns a helper function that takes a target string to evaluate. The pattern supports standard characters, a period to match any single character, and an asterisk to match zero or more of the preceding character. Iterate through the target string and the pattern simultaneously. Check if the next pattern character is an asterisk, and if so, explore both the case where the preceding character is skipped and the case where it consumes a matching character. Check if the pattern character is a period, which successfully consumes any character. Otherwise, verify that the literal characters match exactly, returning a boolean indicating success.

title: Calendar Date Validator
spec: The entry function `validate(date)` receives a string representing a date in year month day format separated by hyphens. Extract the numeric components and verify they form a valid calendar date. Check if the month falls between one and twelve. Determine if the year is a leap year by checking if it is divisible by four, while also checking that it is not divisible by one hundred unless it is also divisible by four hundred. Check if the day is valid for the given month, explicitly checking for months with thirty one days, months with thirty days, and February. Return a boolean indicating if the provided date is strictly valid.

title: Password Strength Analyzer
spec: The entry function `analyze(password)` assesses the strength of a provided string password. Iterate through every character in the password to analyze its composition. Check if the character is an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a numeric digit, or a special punctuation mark, updating a separate flag for each. Check if the total length is at least eight characters, and provide a bonus point if it exceeds twelve characters. Check if the password consists entirely of letters or entirely of numbers to deduct points. Return an integer score from zero to seven based on how many of these conditional checks are satisfied.

title: Robot Maze Navigator
spec: The entry function `navigate(instructions)` receives a list of characters representing commands for a robot on a grid. The robot starts at origin facing north. Iterate through each command in the sequence. Determine if the command is a forward move, and if so, check the current facing direction to update either the vertical or horizontal position accordingly. Check if the command is a left turn to rotate the cardinal direction counterclockwise. Check if the command is a right turn to rotate the direction clockwise. Check if the command is to wait, which does nothing. Check if an unknown command appears, and if so, stop processing immediately. Return a tuple of the final coordinates.

title: Run Length Text Compressor
spec: The entry function `compress(text)` takes a string of alphabetical characters and returns its compressed representation. Initialize an empty result list and a counter. Iterate through the characters of the string using a loop. Check if the current character is identical to the previous character to increment the counter. If the character is different, check if the counter is greater than one to append the count and the previous character to the result, or just the character if the count is exactly one. After the loop finishes, check if there are remaining characters and append the last accumulated character and its count. Return the concatenated result string.

title: Progressive Tax Calculator
spec: The entry function `calculate(income)` receives a floating point number representing an annual income and calculates the total tax owed. The tax system uses many progressive brackets. Check if the income exceeds two hundred fifty thousand to apply a forty percent rate to the excess. Check if the remaining income exceeds one hundred fifty thousand to apply a thirty five percent rate. Check thresholds for one hundred thousand, seventy five thousand, fifty thousand, twenty five thousand, and ten thousand, applying decreasing percentage rates to each slice. Any income below ten thousand is not taxed. Sum the calculated amounts from all applicable brackets and return the total tax rounded to two decimal places.

title: Tic Tac Toe Validator
spec: The entry function `evaluate(board)` receives a list of three lists, each containing three strings that are either empty, ex, or oh. Check all three horizontal rows to see if any row contains three identical non empty symbols. Check all three vertical columns in the same manner. Check the two main diagonals to determine if either has three matching symbols. If any of these directional conditions are met, return the winning symbol. If no winner is found, iterate through all cells using nested loops to check if any empty spaces remain. Return a draw status string if the board is completely full, or a pending status if empty spaces exist.

title: Roman Numeral Converter
spec: The entry function `convert(number)` takes an integer between one and three thousand nine hundred ninety nine and converts it to a roman numeral string. Use a loop to repeatedly subtract the largest possible roman numeral values while building the string. Check if the number is greater than or equal to one thousand to append a thousand symbol. Check if the number is greater than or equal to nine hundred to append a nine hundred symbol. Continue checking specific thresholds for five hundred, four hundred, one hundred, ninety, fifty, forty, ten, nine, five, and four. Subtract the respective amount each time a condition is met until the number reaches zero.

title: Pagination Display Generator
spec: The entry function `paginate(current)` receives the current page number and the total number of pages as integers, and returns a list of strings representing page links to display. Check if the current page is less than one or greater than the total, returning an error string. Check if the total pages are less than or equal to seven, in which case return all pages. Otherwise, check if the current page is within the first four pages to show the first five pages, an ellipsis, and the last page. Check if the current page is within the last four pages to show the first page, an ellipsis, and the last five pages. If none apply, show the first page, an ellipsis, the current page and its neighbors, another ellipsis, and the last page.

title: Chess Pawn Move Validator
spec: The entry function `validate(move)` receives a tuple containing the starting and ending coordinates of a pawn move. Check if the piece is white to evaluate upward board movement. For a white pawn, check if the move is a single step forward into an empty square, or check if it is a double step forward from the second rank. Check if the move is a diagonal capture of a black piece to the left or right. For a black piece, evaluate the downward movement by checking if it moves a single step forward, check if it moves a double step from the seventh rank, or check if it captures diagonally. Return a boolean indicating whether the proposed move strictly follows all pawn rules.

title: Simplified JSON Tokenizer
spec: The entry function `tokenize(text)` processes a string containing a simplified data serialization format and returns a list of string tokens. Iterate through each character using a while loop. Check if the character is a curly brace or square bracket to emit a structural token. Check if the character is a double quote to start reading a string literal, using an inner loop to read until the closing quote is found. Check if the character is a digit or a minus sign to read a numeric sequence. Check if the character is a space, tab, or newline to safely ignore it. Return the final list of extracted tokens.

title: Traffic Intersection Simulator
spec: The entry function `simulate(cars)` receives an integer representing the number of waiting cars. Simulate a traffic light cycle using a loop that decrements a timer. Check if the light is currently green, which allows two cars to pass per time step. Check if the light is yellow, which allows one car to pass only if fewer than two cars are left in the queue. Check if the light is red, during which no cars can pass. Check if an emergency vehicle override is active to immediately turn the light green for one step. Check when the timer for a state reaches zero to transition to the next color in the sequence. Return the total time steps required.

title: English Pluralization Engine
spec: The entry function `pluralize(word)` receives a singular english noun as a string and returns its plural form. Check if the word is an irregular noun like child, mouse, tooth, foot, or person by matching exactly, and return the unique plural. Check if the word ends with a letter why preceded by a consonant, and if so, replace the why with ies. Check if the word ends with the letters ess, ex, zee, see aitch, or ess aitch, and if so, append es. Check if the word ends with an eff or eff ee, and replace the ending with ves. For all other standard cases, simply append an ess to the end of the word.

title: Elevator Route Controller
spec: The entry function `route(requests)` manages an elevator receiving a list of requested floor integers. The elevator starts at floor zero. Loop through the requests to process them sequentially. Check if the requested floor is above the current floor to move the elevator up one floor at a time. Check if the requested floor is below the current floor to move the elevator down. During movement, check if any other pending requests fall exactly on the current floor to stop and service them immediately, removing them from the queue. Check if the elevator is already on the requested floor to just open the doors. Return a list of floors visited.

title: Subtitle Time Shifter
spec: The entry function `shift(subtitles)` receives a string of subtitle text and a time offset in milliseconds. Process the text line by line using a loop. Check if a line is a purely numeric index, and keep it unchanged. Check if a line contains a timestamp arrow sequence to parse the start and end times. Add the time offset to both parsed times. Check if the newly adjusted start time is less than zero, and if so, clamp it to zero. Check if the newly adjusted end time is less than the start time, and if so, force it to equal the start time. Reconstruct the file and return the modified subtitle string.

title: Server Log Anomaly Detector
spec: The entry function `detect(logs)` analyzes a list of strings representing system log entries. Iterate over each log entry to track events and timestamps. Check if the entry contains an error keyword, and if so, increment a dedicated error counter. Check if the entry contains a warning keyword associated with a guest user account, and flag the session. Check if the time difference between consecutive entries exceeds five minutes, which indicates a network timeout. Check if the error counter exceeds three within a ten minute sliding window to generate an alert. Return a summary list of all generated alerts, flags, and timeouts.

title: Blackjack Dealer AI
spec: The entry function `deal(deck)` receives a list of strings representing playing cards and simulates a dealer hand. Continually draw cards from the deck using a loop while the hand value is less than seventeen. Check if a drawn card is an ace, which initially counts as eleven points. Check if the card is a face card like a king, queen, or jack, which counts as ten points. Check if the card is a numeric string to add its exact integer value. After adding a card, check if the total score exceeds twenty one, and if so, check if the hand contains an ace currently valued at eleven to reduce its value to one. Return the final hand score.

title: Semantic Version Comparator
spec: The entry function `compare(versions)` receives two strings representing software versions separated by dots and compares them. Split both strings into components and iterate over them simultaneously. Check if the major version of the first is greater than the second to return one, or check if it is smaller to return negative one. Check the minor version in the exact same way if the major versions match. Check the patch versions if both prior parts are identical. Check if either version contains a pre release alphabetical suffix, noting that a version with a suffix is always considered older than the same version without one. Return zero if they are completely identical.

title: Markdown Table Formatter
spec: The entry function `format(table)` takes a list of strings representing an unaligned text table and aligns its columns. Iterate through all rows to split them by the pipe character and strip whitespace to find the maximum width of each column. Iterate through the rows again to construct the aligned output. Check if a row is a header separator row consisting only of hyphens, and pad it with dashes to match the maximum column width. Check if it is a standard data row, and pad the text with spaces. Check if a column is the very last one in the row to omit the trailing separator spacing. Return the joined table string.

title: Text Word Wrapper
spec: The entry function `wrap(words)` receives a list of string words and an integer line length limit. Initialize an empty line and a list of output lines. Iterate through each word in the list. Check if adding the word to the current line would exceed the character length limit. If it does, check if the current line is completely empty, which implies the single word itself is longer than the limit. Check if this overly long word can be hyphenated by splitting it precisely at the limit. Otherwise, append the current line to the output and start a new line with the current word. Return a single string joined by newline characters.

title: Insurance Premium Calculator
spec: Write a function `premiums(profiles)` that calculates car insurance costs. The input is a list of tuples containing driver age, number of accidents, and car type string. Process the list until a driver age of zero is encountered. The base rate is five hundred. If the age is under twenty five, add two hundred. If the age is over sixty five, add one hundred. If accidents are greater than two, deny coverage by returning zero for that profile. If there is one accident, add one hundred. If there are two accidents, add two hundred fifty. If the car type is sports, add three hundred. If the car type is minivan, subtract fifty. Return a list of final premium amounts. Example: an input of [(20, 1, 'sports'), (70, 3, 'sedan'), (0, 0, 'none')] should output [1100, 0].

title: Shipping Cost Estimator
spec: Write a function `shipping(packages)` that estimates freight costs. The input is a list of tuples with weight in pounds, distance in miles, priority boolean, and international boolean. Process the list until a negative weight is found. The base rate is five. If weight is under two, the weight fee is zero. If weight is between two and ten, add three. If over ten, add ten. If distance is over one thousand, add five. If distance is over three thousand, add fifteen instead. If international is true, add a flat fee of fifty. Finally, if priority is true, double the entire calculated cost for that package. Return a list of costs. Example: input [(1, 500, False, False), (15, 3500, True, False), (-1, 0, False, False)] outputs [5, 60].

title: Library Fine Calculator
spec: Write a function `fines(records)` to calculate overdue library fees. The input is a list of tuples containing a book category string and days overdue. Stop processing and exit the loop when days overdue is negative one. Categories are children, standard, reference, and dvd. Children books always have zero fine. Standard books are ten cents a day, reference books are one dollar a day, and dvd are two dollars a day. The maximum fine for standard is five dollars, reference is ten dollars, and dvd is twenty dollars. If the calculated fine exceeds the maximum, cap it at the maximum. Return a list of fine amounts. Example input: [('standard', 10), ('dvd', 15), ('children', 5), ('none', -1)]. Example output: [1.0, 20.0, 0.0].

title: Bank Loan Approver
spec: Write a function `approve(applications)` that evaluates mortgage applications. The input is a list of tuples with annual income, total debt, and credit score. Process until an income of zero is found. Deny if the credit score is below six hundred. Approve immediately if income exceeds one hundred thousand and debt is below twenty thousand. Otherwise, calculate the debt to income ratio as a percentage. If the ratio is over forty percent, deny. If the credit score is over seven hundred and the ratio is under thirty percent, approve. Otherwise, deny. Return a list of strings: either approved or denied. Example input: [(120000, 10000, 650), (50000, 25000, 710), (0, 0, 0)] outputs ['approved', 'denied'].

title: Hotel Cancellation Fee Calculator
spec: Write a function `penalty(reservations)` to process booking cancellations. The input is a list of tuples holding days notice, room rate, and membership level string. Stop evaluating if days notice is exactly nine hundred ninety nine. Memberships are basic, silver, and gold. Gold members always pay zero fee. Silver members pay half the room rate if notice is under three days, otherwise zero. Basic members pay the full rate if notice is under two days, half the rate if under seven days, and a flat twenty fee if under thirty days. Otherwise, basic members pay zero. Return a list of fee amounts. Example input: [(1, 100, 'basic'), (2, 200, 'silver'), (999, 0, 'none')] outputs [100, 100].

title: Airline Baggage Fee Assessor
spec: Write a function `baggage(bags)` to calculate luggage fees. The input is a list of tuples with weight in pounds, combined dimensions in inches, and passenger status string. Stop processing if weight is zero. Status can be none, elite, or crew. Crew members pay zero. Elite members get one free bag up to fifty pounds, but pay thirty if overweight. For status none, the standard fee is thirty for up to fifty pounds. If weight is between fifty and seventy pounds, the fee is an extra fifty. If weight is over seventy, the bag is not allowed so return negative one. If dimensions exceed sixty two inches, add an oversize fee of seventy five. Return a list of total fees. Example input: [(40, 50, 'elite'), (60, 70, 'none'), (0, 0, 'none')] outputs [0, 155].

title: Coffee Shop Loyalty Program
spec: Write a function `rewards(purchases)` to manage cafe rewards. The input is a list of transaction amounts. Loop through them until a negative transaction is found. For every whole dollar spent, earn one point. If the transaction is exactly five dollars, award two extra bonus points. If the transaction is over twenty dollars, multiply the base points earned for that transaction by two. Keep a running tally of points. Whenever total points reach or exceed one hundred, deduct one hundred points and add one free drink ticket. Return a tuple with total free drinks and remaining points. Example input: [25.50, 5.00, 80.00, -1] outputs (2, 17).

title: Smart Home Thermostat Logic
spec: Write a function `thermostat(readings)` to control home temperature. The input is a list of tuples holding current temperature, target temperature, motion detected boolean, and windows open boolean. Stop processing if current temperature is zero. If windows are open, the action is off. If motion is detected, use the target temperature, else use the target minus five. If the current temperature is at least two degrees lower than the adjusted target, the action is heat. If current is at least two degrees higher than the adjusted target, the action is cool. Otherwise, the action is standby. Return a list of string actions. Example input: [(68, 72, True, False), (70, 72, False, False), (0, 0, False, False)] outputs ['heat', 'cool'].

title: Stock Portfolio Rebalancer
spec: Write a function `rebalance(assets)` to calculate asset trades. The input is a list of tuples with asset class string, current value, and target percentage as a decimal. Process until the asset class is the word stop. First, calculate the total portfolio value of all items before the stop word. Then loop through again. Calculate the current percentage for each asset. If the difference between current and target is less than five percent, the action is zero. If the asset class is bonds and the difference is less than ten percent, the action is zero. If the asset is cash, the action is zero. Otherwise, calculate the dollar amount to buy or sell to reach the exact target. Return a list of dollar amounts rounded to two decimals. Example input: [('stocks', 6000, 0.50), ('bonds', 4000, 0.50), ('stop', 0, 0)] outputs [-1000.0, 0.0].

title: Amusement Park Ride Eligibility
spec: Write a function `screening(riders)` to check rollercoaster restrictions. The input is a list of tuples with height in inches, age in years, and heart condition boolean. Process until height is zero. Deny the rider if heart condition is true. Deny if height is under thirty six inches. If height is under forty eight inches, require a guardian. If age is under ten and height is over forty eight, still require a guardian. Otherwise, approve. Return a list of strings: approved, denied, or guardian. Example input: [(35, 12, False), (40, 8, False), (50, 9, False), (60, 15, True), (0, 0, False)] outputs ['denied', 'guardian', 'guardian', 'denied'].

title: Dietary Restriction Filter
spec: Write a function `filter(menu)` to categorize food safety. The input is a list of tuples with dish name and a list of ingredient strings. Process until the dish name is the word done. Determine if the dish is vegan, gluten free, and nut safe. If it contains meat, poultry, or dairy, it is not vegan. If it contains wheat or barley, it is not gluten free. If it contains peanuts or almonds, it is not nut safe. Return a list of tuples containing the dish name and three booleans representing vegan, gluten free, and nut safe status. Example input: [('salad', ['lettuce', 'almonds']), ('bread', ['wheat', 'water']), ('done', [])] outputs [('salad', True, True, False), ('bread', True, False, True)].

title: Online Shopping Discount Stacker
spec: Write a function `checkout(cart)` to calculate e-commerce totals. The input is a list of tuples with item name, price, category string, and clearance boolean. Stop processing if item name is done. For each item, apply rules to find its final price. If category is electronics, add a five dollar surcharge. If category is clothing and price is over fifty, apply ten percent off that item. If clearance is true, apply twenty percent off that item instead of the clothing discount (clearance takes precedence if both apply). Add the item's final price to a subtotal. After summing all items, if the subtotal is over two hundred, subtract twenty dollars. If under fifty, add ten dollars for shipping. Return the final total. Example input: [('shirt', 60, 'clothing', False), ('tv', 150, 'electronics', True), ('done', 0, '', False)] outputs 169.0.

title: Escape Room Hint Penalty System
spec: Write a function `score(actions)` to evaluate puzzle performance. The input is a list of tuples with action type string and time in minutes. The starting score is one thousand. Stop processing if action type is escape. Action types are minor hint, major hint, and puzzle solved. A minor hint subtracts fifty points. A major hint subtracts one hundred fifty points. A puzzle solved adds fifty points. After processing all actions before escape, look at the time of the escape action. If this time exceeds sixty minutes, subtract ten points for every minute over sixty. If the score drops below zero at any point during calculation, reset it to zero. Return the final score. Example input: [('minor hint', 10), ('puzzle solved', 20), ('major hint', 40), ('escape', 65)] outputs 800.

title: Video Game Matchmaking Rank Adjuster
spec: Write a function `rank(matches)` to compute competitive ratings. The input is a list of tuples with result string, opponent rank, and disconnect boolean. The starting rank is one thousand. Stop processing if result is exit. Result can be win or loss. If disconnect is true, subtract fifty points regardless of the result string. If it is a win and no disconnect, add twenty points, plus an extra ten points if the opponent rank was higher than your current rank. If it is a loss and no disconnect, subtract twenty points, but only subtract ten if the opponent rank was higher. Your rank cannot exceed two thousand and cannot fall below zero. Return the final rank. Example input: [('win', 1200, False), ('loss', 900, False), ('win', 1000, True), ('exit', 0, False)] outputs 960.

title: Traffic Ticket Fine Calculator
spec: Write a function `citations(offenses)` to evaluate driving violations. The input is a list of tuples with speed limit, actual speed, and zone type string. Process until speed limit is zero. Calculate the fine per offense. Speed up to five miles per hour over the limit is a warning with zero fine. Six to fifteen over is one hundred dollars. Sixteen to twenty five over is two hundred dollars. More than twenty five over is four hundred dollars. If the zone type is school, double the calculated fine. If the zone type is construction, add a flat one hundred dollars to the fine. Return a list of fine amounts. Example input: [(30, 34, 'regular'), (50, 70, 'school'), (60, 80, 'construction'), (0, 0, 'none')] outputs [0, 400, 300].

title: Car Rental Price Quote
spec: Write a function `rental(requests)` to process vehicle rentals. The input is a list of tuples with driver age, days rented, car class string, and prepaid fuel boolean. Stop processing if days rented is zero. The base daily rate is thirty for compact, fifty for sedan, and eighty for suv. A driver under twenty five adds a daily fee of twenty. A driver under twenty is completely denied, so return zero for that request. Prepaid fuel adds a flat one time fee of forty for compact, sixty for sedan, and ninety for suv. If days rented exceed seven, apply a ten percent discount to the total cost. Return a list of total costs. Example input: [(22, 3, 'compact', True), (19, 5, 'sedan', False), (0, 0, 'none', False)] outputs [190, 0].

title: Property Tax Assessor
spec: Write a function `taxes(properties)` to evaluate real estate taxes. The input is a list of tuples with property value, property type string, owner age, and disabled boolean. Process until property value is negative one. The base tax is two percent of the property value. If the property type is agricultural, reduce the base tax by half. If the type is commercial, increase it by adding one percent of the property value. If the owner age is over sixty five, subtract five hundred from the tax. If disabled is true, subtract an additional one thousand. If the final tax drops below zero, it becomes zero. Return a list of tax amounts. Example input: [(100000, 'residential', 70, False), (200000, 'agricultural', 40, True), (-1, 'none', 0, False)] outputs [1500.0, 1000.0].

title: Subscription Upgrade Prorater
spec: Write a function `prorate(changes)` to handle software billing. The input is a list of tuples with current plan string, new plan string, and days remaining in the billing cycle. Plans are basic at thirty a month, pro at sixty a month, and max at ninety a month. Stop processing if days remaining is negative. Assume a standard thirty day month to find the daily rate of each plan. If upgrading to a higher rate, charge the difference in daily rates multiplied by days remaining. If downgrading, give a refund of half the difference in daily rates multiplied by days remaining (represented as a negative number). If the plan is the same, the change is zero. Return a list of charges and refunds. Example input: [('basic', 'pro', 10), ('max', 'basic', 15), ('pro', 'pro', 5), ('none', 'none', -1)] outputs [10.0, -15.0, 0.0].

title: Freelance Invoice Generator
spec: Write a function `invoice(logs)` to calculate contractor pay. The input is a list of tuples with hours worked, task type string, and rush boolean. Process until hours worked is zero. The standard rate is fifty per hour. Task types dictate base rates: consulting is standard, development is seventy five per hour, and design is sixty per hour. If rush is true, double the hourly rate for that specific log. If hours worked in a single log exceeds ten, the rate for the hours beyond ten is one point five times the applicable rate. Sum all logs and return the total invoice amount. Example input: [(5, 'development', False), (12, 'design', True), (0, 'none', False)] outputs 1995.0.

title: Event Ticketing Pricing
spec: Write a function `tickets(orders)` to process concert sales. The input is a list of tuples with ticket type string, quantity, and promo code string. Stop if quantity is zero. Ticket types are general for fifty, vip for one hundred, and student for thirty. Calculate the subtotal. If quantity is five or more, apply a ten percent discount to the subtotal. Promo codes apply next: earlybird subtracts ten per ticket from the discounted total, while staff makes the entire order zero. Promo codes do not stack; staff takes priority, and earlybird only applies if the code is exactly earlybird. Return a list of final order prices. Example input: [('vip', 2, 'earlybird'), ('general', 6, 'none'), ('student', 1, 'staff'), ('none', 0, 'none')] outputs [180.0, 270.0, 0.0].

title: Restaurant Tip Calculator
spec: Write a function `gratuity(bills)` to suggest server tips. The input is a list of tuples with bill amount, party size, and service rating string. Process until bill amount is zero. Base tip is fifteen percent. If service rating is excellent, use twenty percent. If rating is poor, use ten percent. If party size is six or more, force an automatic gratuity of eighteen percent regardless of the rating, unless the rating is excellent, in which case keep the twenty percent. Calculate the tip amount based on the bill. If the calculated tip is under two dollars, round it up to two dollars. Return a list of tip amounts. Example input: [(10.0, 2, 'poor'), (100.0, 6, 'good'), (100.0, 8, 'excellent'), (0, 0, 'none')] outputs [2.0, 18.0, 20.0].

title: Gymnastics Scoring System
spec: Write a function `gymnastics(routines)` to judge athletic events. The input is a list of tuples with difficulty score, execution score, fall count, and overtime boolean. Stop processing if difficulty is zero. The base score is difficulty plus execution. Subtract zero point five for each fall. If the fall count is three or more, subtract an extra full point penalty. If overtime is true, subtract zero point one. If the final calculated score exceeds twenty, cap it at exactly twenty. If the score is negative, set it to zero. Return a list of final scores rounded to one decimal place. Example input: [(10.0, 9.5, 1, False), (5.0, 5.0, 4, True), (15.0, 9.0, 0, False), (0, 0, 0, False)] outputs [19.0, 6.9, 20.0].

title: Water Bill Calculator
spec: Write a function `water(readings)` to tally utility costs. The input is a list of tuples with gallons used, customer type string, and late payment boolean. Stop if gallons used is negative one. Customer types are residential and commercial. For residential, the first thousand gallons are free, the next four thousand are two cents per gallon, and anything over five thousand is five cents per gallon. For commercial, there is a base fee of fifty dollars, plus three cents per gallon for all gallons used. After calculating the base bill, if late payment is true, add a ten percent penalty. Return a list of final bills. Example input: [(1500, 'residential', False), (2000, 'commercial', True), (-1, 'none', False)] outputs [10.0, 121.0].

title: Movie Theater Box Office
spec: Write a function `boxoffice(patrons)` to process ticket sales. The input is a list of tuples with age, matinee boolean, and three d boolean. Process until age is zero. The standard base ticket price is fifteen dollars. If age is under twelve, the base price is ten dollars. If age is sixty five or older, the base price is twelve dollars. If matinee is true, subtract three dollars from this base price. If three d is true, add four dollars to the total. The three d surcharge is always four dollars and is never discounted by matinee or age. Accumulate the total revenue for all patrons processed and return that sum. Example input: [(10, True, True), (30, False, True), (70, True, False), (0, False, False)] outputs 39.0.

title: Fitness Tracker Calorie Burn
spec: Write a function `calories(sessions)` to track workouts. The input is a list of tuples with activity type string, duration in minutes, and average heart rate. Process until duration is zero. Activities are running, cycling, swimming, and yoga. Base burn rates per minute are ten for running, eight for cycling, nine for swimming, and four for yoga. For all activities except yoga, modify the rate based on heart rate: if heart rate is over one hundred fifty, increase the base burn rate by twenty percent. If heart rate is under one hundred, decrease it by ten percent. Multiply the final rate by duration. Return a list of total calories burned per session, rounded to the nearest integer. Example input: [('running', 30, 160), ('yoga', 60, 90), ('none', 0, 0)] outputs [360, 240].

title: University Grading Classifier
spec: Write a function `grade(score, late, absence)`. The score is a number, late is a boolean, and absence is an integer. If absence is more than five, the grade is a fail regardless of the score. If late is true, the score drops by ten before checking the grade brackets. If the final score is ninety or above, it is classified as excellent. If the score is between eighty and eighty nine, it is good. If the score is between seventy and seventy nine, it is a pass. Anything below seventy is a fail. Return a string representing the final classification.

title: Fantasy Combat Resolver
spec: Write a function `resolve(attacker, defender)`. Both inputs are lists containing health, attack power, armor, and element type as a string like fire, water, or earth. If the attacker element is fire and defender is earth, increase attack power by fifty percent. If water attacks fire or earth attacks water, also increase the attack by fifty percent. Reduce the final attack power by the defender armor value. If the resulting damage is less than one, set it to one. Subtract the damage from the defender health. If the health falls below zero, set it to zero. Return the updated defender list.

title: Grid Rover Simulator
spec: Write a function `navigate(commands, grid)`. The commands input is a string of letters representing forward, backward, left, and right. The grid is a list of lists of integers where zero is empty space and one is a wall. The rover starts at coordinates zero zero facing east. Loop through each command. If the command is left or right, change the facing direction accordingly. If the command is forward or backward, calculate the new coordinates based on the current facing direction. If the new coordinate is outside the grid boundaries, ignore the move entirely. If the new coordinate contains a wall, stop processing immediately and return the current position. Return a tuple of the final row and column.

title: Network Traffic Firewall
spec: Write a function `filter(packets)`. The input is a list of tuples containing source address, destination port, and protocol string. Create an empty list for allowed traffic and loop through each packet. If the protocol is tcp and the port is eighty or four four three, allow it. If the protocol is udp and the port is fifty three, allow it. If the source address starts with ten dot or one nine two dot, drop it as internal traffic. If the port is twenty two and the source is not a specific trusted address, drop it. Add all allowed items to your list and return it.

title: UNIX Permission Evaluator
spec: Write a function `access(user, file, action)`. The user is a tuple of user id and group id. The file is a tuple of owner id, group id, and an integer representing permission bits. The action is a string like read, write, or execute. First check if the user id matches the file owner id. If so, shift the bits to check the owner permissions. If not, check if the group ids match. If they match, shift the bits for group permissions. If neither match, check the world permissions. If the action is read, check the fours bit. If write, check the twos bit. If execute, check the ones bit. Return a boolean indicating if access is granted.

title: Tabletop Character Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(stats, race, classname)`. Stats is a list of six integers. If any stat is below three or above eighteen, return false. If the race is elf, add two to the second stat. If the race is dwarf, add two to the third stat. If the race is orc, add two to the first and subtract two from the fourth. If the classname is wizard, the fourth stat must be at least fourteen. If the classname is fighter, the first or second stat must be at least fourteen. If the classname is rogue, the second stat must be at least fourteen. Return true if all class requirements are met and stats remain valid.

title: Farm Yield Predictor
spec: Write a function `predict(rainfall, temp, soil)`. Rainfall and temp are numbers, soil is a string. Start with a base yield of one hundred. If rainfall is below twenty, reduce yield by fifty percent. If rainfall is above eighty, reduce yield by twenty percent due to flooding. If temp is below fifteen, subtract thirty from the yield. If temp is above thirty five, subtract forty. If the soil is clay and rainfall is high, subtract another ten. If the soil is sandy and rainfall is low, subtract fifteen. If the soil is loam, add twenty to the final result. Return the final estimated yield as an integer.

title: Rail Fare Calculator
spec: Write a function `price(distance, time, passenger)`. Distance is a number, time is an integer representing hour of day, passenger is a string like adult, child, or senior. Base fare is distance multiplied by zero point two. If the time is between seven and nine or sixteen and eighteen, multiply the fare by one point five for peak hours. If the passenger is a child, apply a fifty percent discount. If the passenger is a senior and it is not peak hours, apply a thirty percent discount. If the calculated fare is less than five, set it to the minimum fare of five. If the distance is over two hundred, subtract ten for a long distance discount. Return the final price rounded to two decimal places.

title: Genetic Sequence Processor
spec: Write a function `analyze(sequence)`. The input is a string of letters. First check if the string length is a multiple of three. If not, return an invalid length error string. Iterate through the string in chunks of three. If a chunk contains any letter other than a, c, g, or t, return an invalid character error. If the chunk is exactly a t g, increment a start counter. If the chunk is t a a, t a g, or t g a, increment a stop counter. If the start counter is zero and a stop chunk is found, return premature stop. If the sequence finishes with no stop chunks, return missing stop. Return a tuple of the two counters.

title: Culinary Recipe Scaler
spec: Write a function `scale(ingredients, multiplier)`. The ingredients input is a list of tuples containing amount, unit, and name. Loop through each item and multiply the amount by the multiplier. If the unit is teaspoon and the new amount is three or more, convert it to tablespoons by dividing by three. If the unit is tablespoon and the amount is sixteen or more, convert it to cups by dividing by sixteen. If the unit is ounces and the amount is sixteen or more, convert it to pounds. If the unit is cup and the amount is more than four, convert to quarts. Return a new list of scaled and converted ingredient tuples.

title: Astrological Sign Finder
spec: Write a function `zodiac(month, day)`. The inputs are two integers. If month is three and day is twenty one or later, or month is four and day is nineteen or earlier, return aries. If month is four and day is twenty or later, or month is five and day is twenty or earlier, return taurus. Continue this pattern for gemini checking may and june, cancer checking june and july, and leo checking july and august. If month is eight and day is twenty three or later, or month is nine and day is twenty two or earlier, return virgo. Return the correct sign string or an error string for completely invalid dates.

title: Metro Commute Assessor
spec: Write a function `commute(zones, transfers, time)`. Zones is an integer, transfers is an integer, time is a float representing the hour. The base cost is two dollars for one zone. If zones is two, add one dollar. If zones is three or more, add two dollars. If the time is between eight and ten in the morning, add a surcharge of fifty cents. If the time is after midnight and before five, add a night fee of one dollar. If transfers is exactly one, add twenty five cents. If transfers is two or more, add fifty cents. If the final total exceeds five dollars, cap it at five dollars. Return the final float value.

title: Dialect Translation Engine
spec: Write a function `translate(sentence)`. The input is a string of words separated by spaces. Split the sentence into words and process each one. If the word starts with a vowel like a, e, i, o, or u, append way to the end. If the word starts with a consonant cluster like ch, sh, or th, move the first two letters to the end and append ay. If the word starts with a single consonant, move it to the end and append ay. If the original word was capitalized, ensure the new word is capitalized. If the word contains numbers, leave it completely unchanged. Join the words back with spaces and return the string.

title: Mountain Resort Lift Access
spec: Write a function `admit(age, passtype, weather)`. Age is an integer, pass type and weather are strings. If weather is blizzard, return closed. If weather is high wind and pass type is beginner, return denied. If age is under five, they must have an adult pass type to ride, otherwise return denied. If age is over sixty five and weather is extreme cold, return a warning string. If the pass type is half day and the current hour is before noon, return wait. If the pass type is VIP, bypass all remaining restrictions and return admitted. Return admitted for all other valid combinations.

title: Greenhouse Irrigation Planner
spec: Write a function `water(moisture, humidity, species)`. Moisture and humidity are percentages as integers, species is a string. If the species is cactus and moisture is above ten, do not water. If the species is fern and moisture is below fifty, water immediately. If humidity is above eighty, reduce the standard watering amount by half. If humidity is below thirty, double the watering amount. If the species is orchid and moisture is below thirty, only water if humidity is also below forty. If the species is tomato and moisture is below forty, water immediately. Return a string indicating whether to water heavily, normally, lightly, or not at all.

title: Multi Rule Text Obfuscator
spec: Write a function `cipher(text, shift)`. The input is a string and an integer. Iterate through each character in the text. If the character is a vowel, shift it forward by the shift amount multiplied by two. If the character is a consonant, shift it forward by the normal shift amount. If the character is a digit, replace it with nine minus the digit. If the character is a space, replace it with an underscore. If the character is punctuation, leave it exactly as it is. If the alphabet shift goes past the letter z, wrap around to the start of the alphabet. Return the fully obfuscated string.

title: Action Game Damage Processor
spec: Write a function `calculate(base, multipliers, conditions)`. Base is an integer, multipliers is a list of floats, conditions is a list of strings. Start with the base damage. If conditions includes stealth, double the damage. If conditions includes poisoned, add five to the base before checking multipliers. Iterate through the multipliers list. If a multiplier is greater than two, cap it at two. If a multiplier is less than zero point five, ignore it completely. Apply each valid multiplier to the running total. If the final damage is over nine thousand, cap it at nine thousand. Return the final integer damage.

title: Intersection Signal Director
spec: Write a function `direct(carsns, carsew, emergency)`. The first two inputs are integers representing waiting cars on north south and east west roads, the third is a boolean. If emergency is true, the north south light turns green and east west turns red immediately. If emergency is false and cars east west are greater than twenty, east west turns green. If cars north south are greater than twenty, north south turns green. If both are greater than twenty, green goes to the direction with the most cars. If both are equal, north south gets priority. If both are zero, switch to a blinking yellow caution state. Return a tuple of two strings representing the north south and east west signal colors.

title: Board Game Word Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(word, squares)`. Word is a string, squares is a list of strings matching the word length indicating special tiles like double letter or triple word. Loop through each character. If the letter is a, e, i, o, or u, its base value is one. If it is z or q, its base value is ten. For other consonants assign standard values. If the corresponding square is double letter, multiply the letter value by two. If it is triple letter, multiply by three. Add the letter values to a running total. Finally, if any square was double word, multiply the entire total by two. If triple word, multiply by three. Return the final integer score.

title: Aviation Delay Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(visibility, wind, traffic)`. Visibility is a number in miles, wind is a number in knots, traffic is an integer representing queued planes. Base delay is zero minutes. If visibility is below three miles, add thirty minutes. If visibility is below one mile, add sixty minutes instead. If wind is above twenty knots, add fifteen minutes. If wind is above forty knots, add forty five minutes. If traffic is between ten and twenty, add ten minutes. If traffic is over twenty, add twenty minutes. If the total delay exceeds one hundred minutes, change the status to canceled. Return a tuple of the delay time and the flight status string.

title: Literary Genre Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify(keywords, length, agerating)`. Keywords is a list of strings, length is an integer page count, age rating is a string like adult or teen. If keywords contains spaceship or alien, set the base genre to sci fi. If keywords contains magic or dragon, set base genre to fantasy. If keywords contains murder or detective, set it to mystery. If the length is under one hundred, append novella to the genre. If the length is over five hundred, append epic. If the age rating is teen, prepend young adult to the output. If no keywords match, return general fiction. Return the constructed genre string.

title: Transaction Anomaly Detector
spec: Write a function `detect(amount, location, time)`. Amount is a float, location is a string country code, time is an integer hour. Set a threat score to zero. If the amount is over one thousand, add three to the score. If the amount is under one dollar, add one to the score. If the location is different from the home country, add four to the score. If the location is a known high risk country, add another two. If the time is between midnight and four in the morning, add three to the score. If the score is five or higher, return blocked. If the score is between three and four, return review. Otherwise return approved.

title: Domestic Animal Diet Planner
spec: Write a function `feed(weight, species, activity)`. Weight is a float in kilos, species is a string, activity is a string like low, medium, or high. Base calories is weight multiplied by thirty. If the species is dog, add ten percent to the base. If the species is cat, subtract five percent. If activity is high, multiply the total by one point five. If activity is low, multiply by zero point eight. If the animal is a puppy or kitten, double the required calories. If the final calorie count is below one hundred, set it to one hundred to prevent starvation. Return the integer rounded calorie requirement.

title: Orbital Module Resource Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(oxygen, power, crew)`. Oxygen and power are percentages, crew is an integer. If crew is zero, switch to standby mode. If oxygen is below twenty percent, trigger a critical alarm. If power is below fifteen percent, turn off non essential systems. If oxygen is dropping faster than expected and crew is more than two, activate backup scrubbers. If power is above ninety percent, charge emergency batteries. If both oxygen and power are below ten percent, initiate evacuation protocols. If all systems are above eighty percent and crew is active, return nominal. Return a string representing the current system status.

title: Photovoltaic Yield Optimizer
spec: Write a function `optimize(sunlight, clouds, temperature)`. Sunlight is a float representing intensity, clouds is a percentage, temperature is degrees celsius. If sunlight is below zero point two, return minimal output. If clouds are above eighty percent, reduce efficiency by fifty percent. If clouds are between fifty and eighty, reduce by twenty percent. If temperature exceeds thirty five degrees, efficiency drops by ten percent due to overheating. If temperature is below zero, efficiency drops by five percent. If sunlight is above zero point eight and clouds are below ten percent, boost expected output by five percent. Return the final efficiency multiplier as a float.

title: Diving Scoring System
spec: Write a function `score(dives)` that calculates the total points for a competition. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a difficulty multiplier, a list of judge scores, a dive position string, and a boolean flag indicating if a balk occurred. Loop through each dive to compute its points. If the dive has five judge scores, discard the single highest and lowest scores. If it has seven scores, discard the two highest and two lowest scores. If a balk occurred, deduct two points from the sum of the remaining scores. If the dive position is straight, add a bonus of one point to the sum. If the position is tucked, subtract half a point. If the dive position is free, add no bonus. If the remaining sum is negative, set it to zero. Finally, multiply the sum by the difficulty multiplier. If the final calculated score exceeds one hundred, cap it at exactly one hundred. Return a list of final scores for all dives evaluated.

title: Ski Jumping Scorer
spec: Implement a function `evaluate(jumps)` to calculate scores for a ski jumping event. The input is a list of tuples containing distance jumped, hill size category as a string, a list of five style scores, wind compensation points, and gate adjustment points. First, calculate the base distance points: start with sixty points for a jump of ninety meters. If the hill is normal size, add two points for every meter over ninety, or subtract two for every meter under. If the hill is large, use one point eight instead of two. If it is a flying hill, use one point two. Next, process the style scores by discarding the highest and lowest values and summing the remaining three. If wind compensation is positive, add it to the distance score. If wind compensation is negative, subtract it. If the starting gate was lowered during the event, add the gate adjustment points. If the gate was raised, subtract them. Add the style points to the adjusted distance points. If the final score is below zero, record it as zero. Return a list of total scores.

title: Cricket Over Simulator
spec: Create a function `simulate(deliveries)` to track runs and wickets in a single over of cricket. The input is a list of strings representing consecutive events. Loop through the events until six valid balls have been bowled. If the event is a wide, add one run to the total but do not count it as a valid ball. If the event is a no ball, add one run, do not count the ball, and mark the next delivery as a free hit. If the event is a wicket, check the free hit status. If a free hit is active, ignore the wicket and reset the free hit. If no free hit is active, increment the wicket count. If the event is a dead ball, ignore it entirely and do not count it. If the event is a boundary four, add four runs and count the ball. If the event is a boundary six, add six runs and count the ball. If the event represents running between wickets, add the numeric value to the total runs and count the ball. A free hit state resets after one valid delivery. Return a tuple of total runs and wickets.

title: Blood Type Compatibility
spec: Write a function `transfuse(requests)` that determines if blood donations are safe. The input is a list of tuples containing the donor blood type, donor rh factor, recipient blood type, and recipient rh factor. Loop through the requests to evaluate compatibility. If the donor is type O and rh negative, automatically mark the donation as safe since they are a universal donor. If the recipient is type AB and rh positive, automatically mark the donation as safe since they are a universal recipient. Otherwise, evaluate specific blood types. If the recipient is type AB, they can receive any ABO type. If the recipient is type O, they can only receive type O. If the recipient is type A, they can receive A or O. If the recipient is type B, they can receive B or O. For the rh factor, if the recipient is positive, they can receive positive or negative blood. If the recipient is negative, they can only receive negative blood. Both ABO and rh conditions must be met for the donation to be safe. Return a list of boolean values for each request.

title: Tarot Card Reader
spec: Design a function `read(spread)` that interprets a tarot reading. The input is a list of tuples containing the suit or category of the card and its orientation, either upright or reversed. Keep a running tally of various life aspects starting at zero. If the category is major arcana, add five to destiny points if upright, or subtract three if reversed. If the category is swords, add two to conflict points. If the category is cups, add two to emotion points. If it is pentacles, add two to material points. If it is wands, add two to passion points. If any minor arcana card is drawn reversed, subtract one from its respective category instead of adding two. If the suit is blank, indicating an unknown card, add one to mystery points. Return a tuple containing the final scores for destiny, conflict, emotion, material, passion, and mystery.

title: Pizza Order Pricer
spec: Build a function `price(orders)` to calculate the total cost of a list of pizza orders. Each order is a tuple containing the size, crust type, and a list of toppings. If the size is small, the base price is ten. If medium, twelve. If large, fifteen. If the crust is stuffed, add two to the base price. If the crust is gluten free, add three. Count the number of toppings: the first two are free, but each additional topping costs one. If the toppings list includes premium items like steak or truffle, add an extra two for each premium item present. If the customer requests extra cheese in the toppings, add one to the price. If the price of a single pizza exceeds twenty, apply a ten percent discount to that specific pizza. Return the grand total sum for all orders in the list.

title: Handball Penalty Assessor
spec: Create a function `assess(fouls)` to determine disciplinary actions in a handball match. The input is a list of tuples describing foul events with the player name, contact type, and severity. Maintain a count of yellow cards and two minute suspensions per player. Loop through the fouls to process them. If the contact is to the head, issue a red card immediately. If the contact is from behind, issue a two minute suspension. If the foul is holding the shirt, issue a yellow card. If the foul involves verbal abuse of the referee, issue a red card. If the foul involves unsportsmanlike conduct, issue a two minute suspension. If the foul is a simple foot block, record it as a free throw with no card. If a player receives a yellow card but already has one, escalate it to a two minute suspension. If a player accumulates three two minute suspensions, escalate the final one to a red card. Return a list of actions taken for each foul in order.

title: Toll Road Billing System
spec: Implement a function `bill(trips)` to calculate charges for vehicles passing through a toll booth. The input is a list of tuples containing vehicle type, number of axles, time of day, and whether they have an electronic pass. Loop through the trips. If the vehicle is an emergency vehicle, the final toll is zero. If the vehicle is a motorcycle, the base toll is one. If it is a car, the base is two. If it is a truck with four axles, the base is five. If the truck has more than four axles, add one for each additional axle. If a trailer is attached to a car, double the base toll. If the vehicle is registered as an electric car, subtract one from the toll. If the time of day is during rush hour, add two to the total. Finally, if the vehicle uses an electronic pass, apply a twenty percent discount to the calculated toll. Return a list of the final tolls.

title: Recycling Center Sorter
spec: Write a function `sort(items)` that categorizes waste for recycling. The input is a list of tuples detailing material, color, and condition. Loop over the items. If the material is glass and the color is clear, categorize it as clear glass. If the glass is green or brown, categorize it as colored glass. If the glass is blue, reject it. If the material is plastic and the type is one or two, categorize it as recyclable plastic. If the plastic type is three through seven, reject it. If the material is paper and it is wet, reject it. If the paper is dry, categorize it as clean paper. If the material is metal and it is aluminum or steel, categorize it as scrap metal. If the material is electronic, categorize it as electronic waste. If the material is biological, reject it completely. Return a list of categorizations or rejections in the same order as the input.

title: Laundry Wash Cycle Selector
spec: Design a function `select(loads)` to choose the appropriate washing machine settings. The input is a list of tuples with fabric type, soil level, and color fastness. Evaluate each load to return a cycle string. If the fabric is silk or wool, select the delicate cycle. If the fabric is denim, select the heavy duty cold cycle. If the load contains waterproof jackets, select the gentle cold cycle. If the fabric is cotton and heavily soiled, select heavy duty warm. If the fabric is synthetic and lightly soiled, select permanent press. If the item is heavily soiled and synthetic, select warm permanent press. If the colors are known to bleed, select the cold wash cycle to prevent fading. If the load consists of white cotton, select the hot wash cycle. For all other combinations, default to a normal warm wash. If the soil level is extreme, append an extra rinse phase to the selected cycle name. Return a list of chosen cycles.

title: Aquarium Tank Balancer
spec: Create a function `balance(readings)` to automate aquarium maintenance. The input is a list of tuples representing current temperature, acidity, salinity, ammonia, nitrate, water level, and filter flow. For each reading, compile a list of necessary adjustments. If the temperature is below seventy five, add a command to turn on the heater. If it is above eighty two, add a command to turn on the chiller. If the acidity is below six point five, add a command to dose alkaline buffer. If the acidity is above seven point five, add a command to dose acid. If salinity drops below one point zero two, add a command to mix salt. If ammonia is strictly greater than zero, immediately append an emergency water change alert. If the nitrate level is above forty, add a command to schedule a routine water change. If the water level is marked as low, add a command to top off the tank. If the filter flow is restricted, add a command to clean the filter media. Return a list of adjustment lists for each reading.

title: Bicycle Gear Advisor
spec: Implement a function `advise(metrics)` that recommends gear shifts for a cyclist. The input is a list of tuples containing current cadence, gradient percentage, speed, terrain type, and rider posture. Evaluate each state to suggest an action. If the rider is sprinting, suggest shifting to the highest gear immediately. If standing on the pedals, suggest maintaining the current gear. If the cadence is above ninety and the gradient is flat, suggest a shift up. If the cadence is below seventy and the gradient is uphill, suggest a shift down. If the speed is over twenty and the gradient is downhill, suggest two shifts up. If the gradient is steep uphill and the speed is dropping rapidly, suggest a front derailleur shift down. If the speed is under five and the cyclist is approaching a stop, suggest shifting down to the lowest gear. If riding on gravel and the speed is high, suggest shifting down once for better torque. If a strong crosswind is detected, suggest shifting down to maintain control. Return a list of suggested actions.

title: Bakery Inventory Manager
spec: Write a function `manage(stock)` to process end of day bakery items. The input is a list of tuples containing item category, age in days, and current quantity. Determine the action for each item. If the category is bread and it is older than two days, mark it for discard. If it is bread and exactly one day old, mark it for a fifty percent discount. If the category is pastry and it is older than one day, discard it immediately. If it is cake and older than three days, discount it by twenty percent. If the cake is older than five days, discard it. If the item is a cookie and older than seven days, discard it. If a cookie is older than three days, discount it by ten percent. If it is a muffin and its age is two days, discount it by thirty percent. If the item is fresh bread and the quantity is below ten, append a bake alert to the action. Return a list of actions corresponding to the input items.

title: Dog Show Evaluator
spec: Develop a function `judge(dogs)` to score competitors in a conformation show. The input is a list of tuples detailing the dog's height, weight, coat color, gait, ear posture, tail docking, and behavior. Start each dog with a perfect score of one hundred. If the height exceeds twenty inches, deduct five points. If the weight is under thirty pounds, deduct three points. If the coat color is non standard, record a disqualification and assign a score of zero. If the dog is pacing instead of trotting, deduct ten points for a movement fault. If the teeth are overshot, deduct two points. If the teeth are undershot, deduct eight points for a major fault. If the ears do not stand erect, deduct four points. If the tail is docked improperly, deduct six points. If the dog acts aggressively towards the judge, disqualify immediately and assign a score of zero. Return a list of final scores for all dogs evaluated.

title: Music Scale Generator
spec: Create a function `generate(parameters)` that builds musical scales. The input is a tuple with a starting note number and a string representing the mode. Start a list with the initial note. Loop exactly seven times to build an octave. If the mode is major, use the interval pattern of two, two, one, two, two, two, one half steps. If the mode is natural minor, use two, one, two, two, one, two, two. If the mode is harmonic minor, use the natural minor pattern but increase the seventh interval by one to create a leading tone. If the mode is melodic minor ascending, raise the sixth and seventh intervals of the natural minor. If the mode is dorian, use two, one, two, two, two, one, two. If the mode is phrygian, use one, two, two, two, one, two, two. If the mode is lydian, use two, two, two, one, two, two, one. Calculate each successive note by adding the current interval to the previous note. Return the list of eight notes.

title: Museum Tour Group Router
spec: Implement a function `route(groups)` to assign paths through a museum for various visitor groups. The input is a list of tuples containing group size, type, special requests, and mobility status. If the group size is over forty, assign them to start in the main hall to prevent overcrowding. If the group is a school field trip, route them through the dinosaur exhibit first. If the group specifically requests ancient history, ensure their route includes the egypt wing. If any members have mobility issues, remove the spiral staircase from their route and replace it with the elevator path. If the tour duration is scheduled for under one hour, skip the contemporary art section entirely to save time. If the group is composed of toddlers, route them to the interactive children wing. If the group is a vip donor tour, include a private vault viewing. If the museum is currently crowded, avoid the main atrium path. Return a list of final route itineraries.

title: Solar Eclipse Forecaster
spec: Write a function `forecast(alignments)` to classify astronomical events. The input is a list of tuples containing the angular distance from the lunar node, the moon distance from earth, solar activity level, and time of day. If the angular distance from the node is greater than ten degrees, no eclipse occurs. If the distance is under ten degrees but the moon is near its apogee, classify it as an annular eclipse. If the moon is near its perigee and perfectly aligned under one degree, classify it as a total eclipse. If the alignment is between one and ten degrees regardless of distance, it is a partial eclipse. If a total eclipse occurs during high solar activity, append a coronal mass ejection viewing alert. If a partial eclipse happens near the horizon, append a atmospheric refraction warning. If an annular eclipse occurs during a supermoon phase, classify it as a hybrid eclipse. If the event happens during a lunar eclipse window instead, return a lunar eclipse classification. Return a list of classifications.

title: Drone Flight Controller
spec: Design a function `control(telemetry)` to output safety commands for an autonomous drone. The input is a list of tuples containing battery percentage, wind speed, distance to restricted airspace, payload weight, gps signal strength, and motor temperature. Process each telemetry frame. If the battery falls below fifteen percent, issue a return to home command. If the battery drops below five percent, issue an emergency land command immediately. If the wind speed exceeds twenty miles per hour, issue a reduce altitude command. If the distance to restricted airspace is under one hundred feet, issue a reverse course command. If the payload is heavy and the battery is draining rapidly, issue a reduce speed command to conserve power. If gps signal is lost, issue a hover in place command. If a collision avoidance sensor triggers, issue an evade upward command. If the motor temperature exceeds safe limits, issue a reduce throttle command. Return a list of generated flight commands.

title: Coffee Roasting Profile
spec: Create a function `roast(logs)` to automate adjustments in a coffee roaster. The input is a sequence of temperature readings, rate of rise, auditory crack events, ambient humidity, and time elapsed. Loop over the logs. If the bean temperature is under two hundred degrees, the roaster is in the drying phase, so set the heat to maximum. If the temperature is between two hundred and three hundred degrees, it enters the maillard phase, so reduce the heat to medium. If the rate of rise spikes above thirty degrees per minute, increase the fan speed to clear smoke. If a first crack event is detected, lower the heat further to prevent scorching the beans. If a second crack event is heard, stop the roast immediately. If the ambient humidity is high, increase the baseline fan speed by ten percent. If the bean temperature stalls for more than one minute, increase the heat to high. If the roast time exceeds fifteen minutes, abort the roast to prevent baked flavors. Return a list of setting adjustments.

title: Miniature Golf Scorer
spec: Implement a function `score(holes)` to calculate a player's round in miniature golf. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list represents the sequence of strokes for a single hole, recorded as strings like hit, water, out of bounds, or sand trap. Loop over each hole. For each stroke, if it is a standard hit, add one to the hole tally. If the stroke goes in the water, add one stroke and a one stroke penalty. If it goes out of bounds, add one stroke and a two stroke penalty. If the stroke hits a sand trap, add one stroke and zero penalties. If the stroke skips over the water hazard successfully, record it as a trick shot and subtract one penalty point. If the total strokes for a hole reach six, cap the score at six and immediately move to the next hole. If the very first stroke is a hit that completes the hole, apply a hole in one bonus by subtracting a point. Sum the hole scores and return the total round score.

title: Plant Watering Schedule
spec: Write a function `schedule(plants)` to determine daily greenhouse tasks. The input is a list of tuples containing plant species, soil moisture level, ambient humidity, forecast rain, and lifecycle stage. Loop through the plants. If the plant is a succulent, only schedule watering if the soil moisture is completely dry and the humidity is low. If it is a tropical plant, schedule watering if the topsoil is dry, regardless of humidity. If it is a fern, schedule watering if the soil is even slightly dry. If rain is forecast in the next twenty four hours, skip watering for any plants marked as outdoor. If the temperature exceeds ninety degrees, water all outdoor non succulents even if the soil is damp. If the plant is a newly propagated cutting, water lightly every single day regardless of soil. If the plant is an orchid, only water if the roots appear silvery gray. If the plant is dormant for the winter, skip watering entirely. Return a list of plants needing water.

title: Warehouse Storage Locator
spec: Design a function `locate(items)` to assign warehouse bays to incoming freight. The input is a list of tuples detailing item weight, hazard class, refrigeration requirements, turnover rate, and fragility. Loop through the items. If the item is hazardous and flammable, assign it to the outdoor bunker. If it is hazardous and toxic, assign it to the secure locked cage. If the item requires refrigeration, assign it to the cold storage zone. If the item weighs over one hundred pounds, assign it to the bottom rack to prevent lifting injuries. If the item is lightweight and has a high turnover rate, assign it to the front shelves for easy access. If the item is oversized and cannot fit on a rack, assign it to floor loading. If the item is fragile, assign it to the padded safety shelves. If the item is high value, assign it to the security vault. If the item is biological material, assign it to the quarantine zone. Return a list of bay assignments.

title: Boarding Pass Assigner
spec: Implement a function `board(passengers)` to organize airline boarding groups. The input is a list of tuples containing passenger mobility needs, military status, ticket class, frequent flyer tier, and age. Evaluate each passenger. If a passenger requires a wheelchair or extra time, assign them to group one. If the passenger is active duty military, also assign them to group one. If the passenger is flying in first class, assign them to group two. If they hold elite frequent flyer status, assign them to group three. If the passenger is traveling with an infant, assign them to group four. If they hold a basic economy ticket with no overhead bin access, assign them to group six. If the passenger is an unaccompanied minor, assign them to group one and flag for escort. If the passenger purchased priority boarding as an add on, assign them to group three. If the passenger is traveling with a pet in cabin, assign them to group five and flag for inspection. Otherwise, assign them to group five. Return a list of boarding groups.

title: Snowplow Route Planner
spec: Create a function `plow(roads)` to prioritize snow clearing operations. The input is a list of tuples specifying road type, current snow depth, hospital route status, time of day, and weather alerts. Loop over the roads. If the road is an arterial highway and snow depth is over two inches, assign it priority one. If the road is a designated hospital route, assign it priority one regardless of the snow depth. If the road is residential and the snow depth exceeds six inches, assign it priority two. If a residential road has under six inches of snow, assign it priority three. If the time of day is between midnight and five in the morning, suspend all priority three plowing and reassign them to standby status. If the road is a school bus route and the time is between six and eight in the morning, elevate to priority one. If the road is a steep hill and icing is reported, dispatch a salt truck before the plow. If a snow emergency is declared by the city, upgrade all residential roads to priority two. Return a list of assigned priorities.

title: Archery Tournament Scorer
spec: Write a function `evaluate(arrows)` to score an archer's target practice. The input is a list of tuples containing the ring hit, a boolean indicating if it broke the line into the next ring, and sequence penalties. For each arrow, if it hits the center x ring, score it as ten points and record an x for tie breaking. If it hits the inner gold, award ten points. If it hits the outer gold, award nine points. If it hits the inner red, award eight. If it hits the outer red, award seven. If it hits the inner blue, award six. If it hits the outer blue, award five. If the arrow is a line breaker, increment its score by one to award the higher ring value, up to a maximum of ten. If the arrow misses the target entirely, award zero points. If the archer shoots out of sequence, deduct two points from the total. If the arrow bounces off the target face, record it as a re shoot instead of assigning points. Return a tuple containing the total score and the count of x ring hits.

title: Darts Match Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(throws)` that calculates the remaining score in a game of darts starting from five hundred and one. The input is a list of tuples containing the target segment and a multiplier. A standard target is a number from one to twenty, which can have a multiplier of one, two, or three. The outer bullseye has a value of twenty-five and a multiplier of one, while the inner bullseye has a value of fifty and a multiplier of one. Subtract the value of each throw multiplied by its multiplier from the current score. If a throw reduces the score to exactly zero and has a multiplier of two or is the inner bullseye, the game is won. If a throw reduces the score to one, or below zero, or to exactly zero without a multiplier of two or inner bullseye, the throw is a bust and the score reverts to what it was before that turn began. Return the final score as an integer, or a string indicating a win. For example, passing throws of twenty with a multiplier of three, and twenty with a multiplier of one returns four hundred and twenty one.

title: Tennis Game Tracker
