spec: Implement a function `track(points)` that takes a list of strings indicating which player won each point, either player one or player two. Both players start at zero points. Winning a point progresses their score from zero to fifteen, then thirty, then forty. If both players reach forty, the game enters deuce. From deuce, if a player wins a point, they gain the advantage. If the player with the advantage wins the next point, they win the game. If the other player wins the point instead, the score returns to deuce. If a player reaches forty and wins the next point while the other player is at thirty or less, they win the game outright. Return a string representing the current state of the game, such as player one wins, player two wins, deuce, advantage player one, advantage player two, or the numerical score like fifteen to thirty. For example, a sequence of four points won by player one returns the string player one wins.

title: Rugby Match Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(events)` that calculates the final points for two opposing rugby teams. The input is a list of tuples containing the scoring team as an integer one or two, and the event type as a string. A try awards five points. If a try is scored, the very next event might be a conversion by the same team, which awards two points. If a conversion is missed or the team scores something else next, no extra points are added for the conversion. A penalty kick awards three points. A drop goal awards three points. If an event type is a yellow card, the offending team loses one point as a disciplinary deduction. If an event type is a red card, they lose three points. If the total points for a team drops below zero due to penalties, cap their score at zero. Keep a running tally for both teams. Return a tuple containing the final score of team one and team two.

title: Ski Pass Pricing Estimator
spec: Write a function `price(attributes)` that calculates the cost of a daily ski pass. The base price is one hundred dollars. The input is a list containing the skier's age, the season, the days booked in advance, whether they are a local resident, and whether they are a student. If the age is under twelve or over sixty-five, apply a fifty percent discount to the base price. If the season is peak, add a twenty dollar surcharge, but if it is spring, deduct ten dollars. If the ticket is booked more than thirty days in advance, apply a twenty percent discount on the current subtotal, or if it is booked between seven and thirty days in advance, apply a ten percent discount. Finally, if the skier is a local resident, deduct fifteen dollars from the total. If they are a student, deduct ten dollars. Only one of the resident or student discounts can be applied, preferring the resident discount. Return the final price rounded to the nearest dollar.

title: Wind Turbine Output Calculator
spec: Design a function `calculate(conditions)` that estimates the power output of a wind turbine in kilowatts based on a list of conditions containing wind speed in meters per second, temperature in celsius, and a maintenance flag. The turbine has a rated capacity of two thousand kilowatts. If the maintenance flag is true, the output is immediately zero. If the wind speed is below three meters per second, it is too low to generate power, so the output is zero. If the wind speed is between three and twelve meters per second, the output increases proportionally from zero to the maximum two thousand kilowatts. If the wind speed is between twelve and twenty-five meters per second, the output is exactly two thousand kilowatts. If the wind speed exceeds twenty-five meters per second, the turbine brakes for safety, and the output is zero. Furthermore, if the temperature is below zero degrees, reduce the final output by ten percent due to icing, and if the temperature is above thirty-five degrees, reduce it by five percent to prevent overheating. Return the calculated power as a float.

title: Fishing Catch Validator
spec: Implement a function `validate(catch)` that checks if a caught fish is legal to keep. The input is a list containing the species name, length in centimeters, the current month, the location type, and the angler license tier. For a salmon, the length must be at least fifty centimeters, and it can only be caught between May and September inclusive. For a bass, the length must be between thirty and forty-five centimeters, and it is illegal to catch in marine locations. For a trout, the length must be at least twenty-five centimeters, and catching them requires a premium license tier. If the location type is protected, all fishing is strictly catch and release regardless of species. If any of these conditions are violated, return a string indicating the specific reason for rejection, such as undersized, out of season, protected area, or insufficient license. If all rules are satisfied, return the string approved.

title: Sailing Race Handicapper
spec: Write a function `handicap(data)` that calculates the corrected time for a sailboat in a race. The input is a list containing the boat class, elapsed time in minutes, average wind speed in knots, a false start penalty flag, and the number of buoys touched. The base corrected time is the elapsed time. If the boat class is laser, multiply the time by a rating of zero point nine. If the class is catamaran, multiply by zero point eight. If the class is dinghy, multiply by one point one. Next, adjust for wind conditions. If the wind speed is below five knots, add a five percent penalty to the time because heavier boats struggle more. If the wind speed is above twenty knots, subtract five percent from the time. Add five minutes to the time for every buoy touched. Finally, if the false start flag is true, add an additional ten minutes to the time. Return the final corrected time rounded to one decimal place.

title: Spacecraft Status Monitor
spec: Create a function `monitor(telemetry)` that evaluates the health of a descending spacecraft. The input is a list of five numbers representing altitude in kilometers, velocity in meters per second, heat shield temperature in celsius, fuel percentage, and communication signal strength. Start with an empty list of warning messages. If altitude is below fifty and velocity is greater than two thousand, append a velocity warning. If the heat shield temperature exceeds one thousand five hundred, append a critical temperature warning, or if it is below minus fifty, append a freezing warning. If the fuel percentage drops below ten, append a low fuel warning. If the communication signal strength is below twenty, append a signal loss warning. If the list of warnings is empty, check if altitude is zero and velocity is less than ten, and if so return a list containing only a safe landing message, otherwise return a list containing only nominal. Otherwise, return the accumulated list of warnings.

title: Baking Recipe Adjuster
spec: Implement a function `adjust(recipe)` that modifies a baking time and temperature based on environmental factors. The input is a list containing the original baking time in minutes, original temperature in fahrenheit, altitude in feet, humidity percentage, and the pan material. If the altitude is above five thousand feet, increase the temperature by twenty-five degrees and decrease the baking time by ten percent. Alternatively, if the altitude is above three thousand feet, increase the temperature by fifteen degrees and decrease the baking time by five percent. If the original temperature is above four hundred degrees, halve these altitude temperature increases. If the humidity is above eighty percent, increase the baking time by three minutes to account for extra moisture, unless the original baking time is under ten minutes, in which case ignore humidity. If the pan material is glass, decrease the final temperature by twenty-five degrees because glass retains heat better. If the pan material is dark metal, decrease the temperature by ten degrees. Return a list containing the adjusted time rounded to the nearest minute and the adjusted temperature rounded to the nearest degree.

title: Ferry Loading Organizer
spec: Write a function `load(vehicles)` that calculates the layout of vehicles on a ferry. The input is a list of tuples containing vehicle type, length in meters, weight in tons, and a hazardous cargo flag. The ferry has a main deck with a fifty meter lane and a lower deck with a forty meter lane, and a total weight capacity of one hundred tons. If a vehicle has hazardous cargo, it must be placed on the main deck regardless of size. If the vehicle is a truck and weighs more than ten tons, it must also go on the main deck. If the vehicle is a passenger car, it prefers the lower deck. If the preferred or required deck is full, meaning the sum of lengths exceeds the lane capacity, it attempts to go to the other deck, unless it is restricted. If both decks are full or restricted, the vehicle is rejected. If the vehicle's weight alone exceeds the remaining total weight capacity of the ferry, it is rejected. Return a list of tuples containing the accepted vehicles and their assigned decks.

title: Car Wash Controller
spec: Create a function `wash(settings)` that generates a sequence of washing stages. The input is a list containing the package type, dirt level, and vehicle size. The available packages are basic, standard, and premium. Always start the sequence with an undercarriage spray. If the dirt level is high, append a heavy pre-soak stage, otherwise append a standard pre-soak, unless the package is basic and the dirt level is low and the size is small, in which case skip the pre-soak entirely. Next, append a soap application. If the vehicle size is large, append an extended scrubbing stage, otherwise append a regular scrubbing stage. After scrubbing, append a high pressure rinse. If the package is standard or premium, append a tire cleaning stage and a wax application. If the package is premium, additionally append a ceramic coating stage. Finally, if the vehicle size is small, append a standard dry, but if the vehicle size is large or the package is premium, append an extended heated dry. Return the list of stages in order.

title: Smart Blinds Optimizer
spec: Implement a function `optimize(sensors)` that determines the optimal tilt angle for motorized window blinds. The input is a list containing sun elevation angle, indoor temperature, target temperature, outdoor temperature, and wind speed. If the wind speed exceeds forty kilometers per hour, the blinds must be fully retracted for safety, returning the string retracted. Otherwise, if the sun elevation is below zero, meaning it is night, the blinds should be fully closed at zero degrees to conserve heat. During the day, if the indoor temperature is greater than the target temperature and the outdoor temperature is higher than the indoor temperature, tilt the blinds to ninety degrees to block sunlight. If the indoor temperature is less than the target temperature and the outdoor temperature is higher, tilt the blinds to forty-five degrees to let sunlight in for passive heating. In all other cases, keep the blinds at a neutral open angle of forty-five degrees to allow natural light. Return the numerical angle or the string retracted.

title: Submarine Sonar Classifier
spec: Create a function `classify(contacts)` that evaluates an array of underwater sonar contacts. The input is a list of tuples containing signal strength, acoustic frequency in hertz, movement speed in knots, and depth in meters. If the signal strength is below ten, ignore the contact as background noise and do not add it to the results. If the speed is zero and depth is exactly zero, classify it as a surface buoy. If the speed is above thirty knots and depth is greater than fifty meters, classify it as a torpedo. If the frequency is between twenty and fifty hertz and the speed is between five and fifteen knots, classify it as a whale. If the frequency is above one thousand hertz and the depth is less than twenty meters, classify it as a small watercraft. If the speed is between ten and twenty knots, the depth is below one hundred meters, and the frequency is below two hundred hertz, classify it as a submarine. For any other combination that is not ignored, classify it as an unknown anomaly. Return a list of classifications in the order the valid contacts were received.

title: Paint Color Dispenser
spec: Create a function `dispense(order)` that calculates the required amounts of base paint and colorants in milliliters. The input is a list containing the desired color name, the finish type, and the total volume requested. Start with the entire volume as the base paint. If the finish is gloss, subtract ten percent of the volume from the base and assign it to gloss additive. If the finish is matte, subtract five percent from the base for a flattening agent. If the finish is satin, subtract two percent for a smoothing agent. If the color is crimson, add ten milliliters of red colorant and two milliliters of blue colorant for every liter of total volume requested. If the color is mint, add five milliliters of green and one milliliter of yellow per liter. If the color is navy, add twelve milliliters of blue and three milliliters of black per liter. If the color is mustard, add eight milliliters of yellow and two of brown per liter. If the total requested volume is over twenty liters, apply a five percent bulk discount reduction to the colorant amounts added. Ensure the base paint volume is finally adjusted by subtracting the total volume of all added colorants. Return a list of tuples containing the ingredient names and their calculated volumes.

title: Helicopter Preflight Checker
spec: Implement a function `check(parameters)` that verifies if a helicopter is safe to take off. The input is a list containing main rotor RPM, tail rotor RPM, engine temperature in celsius, oil pressure in PSI, and wind speed in knots. If the engine temperature is below forty degrees, return a message to warm up the engine. If the engine temperature is above one hundred and ten degrees, return a message to shut down due to overheating. If the oil pressure is below fifty PSI, return a low oil pressure warning. If the wind speed exceeds thirty-five knots, return a weather hold message. If the main rotor RPM is below three hundred, or the tail rotor RPM is below one thousand five hundred, return a spooling up message indicating they have not reached flight speed. If all these checks pass, and the wind speed is between twenty and thirty-five knots, return a marginal weather caution message. If all checks pass and winds are calm, return clear for takeoff.

title: Telescope Alignment Calibrator
spec: Write a function `calibrate(observation)` that determines adjustments for an automated telescope. The input is a list containing the target type, tracking mode, atmospheric seeing quality, installed filter, and moon phase. The target types are planet, nebula, or galaxy. If the target is a planet, set the focal length to long and tracking to planetary. If the target is a nebula or galaxy, set the focal length to short and tracking to sidereal. If the atmospheric seeing is poor, append an instruction to activate adaptive optics. If the seeing is excellent, append an instruction to bypass adaptive optics. If the target is a nebula and the filter is none, append an instruction to insert a narrowband filter. If the target is a planet and the filter is narrowband, append an instruction to switch to a color filter. If the filter installed is infrared and the target is not a planet, append an instruction to remove the infrared filter. If the target is a galaxy and the moon phase is full, append a light pollution warning. If the provided tracking mode does not match the required tracking determined by the target, append a tracking mismatch warning. Return a list of all determined instructions and warnings.

title: Server Rack Power Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(sensors)` that manages the power states of a server rack. The input is a list of lists, where each sublist represents a server and contains the server string identifier, CPU usage percentage, current power draw in watts, and temperature in celsius. The rack has a maximum power capacity of five thousand watts. First, calculate the total power draw. If the total draw exceeds the capacity, find the active server with the highest power draw and append a shutdown command for its identifier. If a server's temperature exceeds eighty-five degrees, append a thermal throttle command for that server. If a server's temperature exceeds ninety-five degrees, append an emergency shutdown command regardless of power limits. If a server has less than five percent CPU usage but draws more than two hundred watts, append a sleep command to save energy. If the total power draw is below three thousand watts and any server is previously known to be in sleep mode, append a wake command. Return the list of issued commands.

title: Snooker Break Scorer
spec: Implement a function `score(balls)` that calculates the points scored in a single continuous turn of snooker. The input is a list of strings representing the colors of the balls potted in order. A red ball is worth one point, yellow two, green three, brown four, blue five, pink six, and black seven. The sequence must alternate between red and any other color. If a red is expected but a non-red is potted, the break ends immediately and no points are added for that foul shot. If a color is expected but a red is potted, the break also ends. Once all reds are gone, which you can assume is after exactly fifteen reds have been potted in the break, the colors must be potted in strictly ascending order of their value. If a ball is potted out of sequence during this final phase, the break ends. Accumulate the values of all legally potted balls and return the total score as an integer.

title: Fencing Bout Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(actions)` that determines the points awarded in a fencing exchange. The input is a list of strings representing a sequence of actions, such as attack left, attack right, parry left, parry right, touch left, touch right, and off target. In foil fencing, a touch only scores if the fencer has right of way. An attack establishes right of way for that fencer. A parry transfers right of way to the defender. If a fencer with right of way lands a touch, they score one point and the exchange ends. If they land an off target, the exchange ends with no points. If a fencer lands a touch without right of way, it is ignored unless the fencer with right of way missed completely or went off target. If both attack simultaneously without a parry and both touch, it is a simultaneous action and no points are awarded. Process the sequence to track right of way and return a tuple of points scored by the left fencer and the right fencer.

title: Figure Skating Evaluator
spec: Create a function `evaluate(routine)` that calculates the technical score for a figure skating program. The input is a list of tuples, each containing an element name, a base value, a grade of execution from minus five to plus five, and a fall flag. For each element, start with the base value. If the grade of execution is positive, add ten percent of the base value for each grade point. If the grade of execution is negative, subtract ten percent of the base value for each grade point. If the fall flag is true, subtract a mandatory one point from the element's score, and cap the grade of execution at a maximum of minus three before calculating its penalty. If an element's final score drops below zero, set it to zero. Furthermore, if the element name contains the word jump and occurs in the second half of the routine, indicated by being past the middle index of the list, multiply its base value by one point one before applying execution grades. Return the total score rounded to two decimal places.

title: Photography Exposure Adviser
spec: Implement a function `advise(scene)` that recommends camera settings based on scene characteristics. The input is a list containing the light level in lux, subject speed in kilometers per hour, and desired depth of field as shallow or deep. Start with an ISO of one hundred, an aperture of point f eight, and a shutter speed of one two hundredth of a second. If the subject speed is above fifty, change the shutter speed to one one thousandth and increase the ISO to eight hundred. If the subject speed is between ten and fifty, change the shutter speed to one five hundredth and increase the ISO to four hundred. If the subject speed is zero, change the shutter speed to one fiftieth. Next, adjust for depth of field. If shallow is desired, change the aperture to point f two point eight and halve the ISO, ensuring it does not drop below one hundred. If deep is desired, change the aperture to point f sixteen and double the ISO. Finally, if the light level is below one thousand lux, double the ISO again. If the light level is below one hundred lux, require a tripod and change the shutter speed to one full second, while setting the aperture to point f one point four. Return a list of the final ISO, aperture, and shutter speed.

title: Baggage Routing Sorter
spec: Write a function `route(baggage)` that determines the correct conveyor chute for a piece of luggage. The input is a list containing the destination code, weight in kilograms, length in centimeters, priority class, a fragile flag, and security scan status. If the security scan status is fail, immediately route the bag to the manual inspection chute regardless of other attributes. If the length exceeds one hundred and twenty centimeters or the weight exceeds thirty-two kilograms, route the bag to the oversized freight chute. If the bag is tagged as fragile and is not oversized, route it to the fragile handling belt regardless of its destination code. For normal bags, if the priority class is first or business, append the priority tag to the routing instruction. If the priority class is economy but the weight is less than ten kilograms, append an express tag. If the destination code is local, meaning it starts with the letter L, route it to carousel one. If the destination code is domestic, starting with D, route it to carousel two. If the destination code is international, starting with I, route it to carousel three. Return a string combining the tag if applicable and the destination carousel or chute name.

title: Electric Vehicle Charger Negotiator
spec: Create a function `negotiate(status)` that determines the charging current in amps for an electric vehicle. The input is a list containing the current battery percentage, battery temperature in celsius, cable max rating in amps, and the station power limit in amps. The absolute maximum current is the lower of the cable rating and the station limit. If the battery temperature exceeds forty-five degrees, the current must be set to zero for safety. If the temperature is below zero degrees, the current is limited to a maximum of ten amps to prevent lithium plating. If the temperature is safe, look at the battery percentage. If the percentage is above eighty, the current is limited to twenty amps to protect battery health. If the percentage is above ninety-five, the current is limited to five amps for trickle charging. If the percentage is below eighty and the temperature is safe, allow the absolute maximum current. Return the final negotiated current as an integer.

title: Cheese Aging Tracker
spec: Implement a function `track(cheese)` that prescribes daily care tasks for a cheese wheel. The input is a list containing the cheese type, age in weeks, current humidity percentage, and mold presence flag. If the cheese type is brie, and the age is less than two weeks, append a turn daily instruction. If the type is brie and the humidity is below ninety percent, append an increase humidity instruction. If the cheese type is cheddar, and the age is less than four weeks, append a turn weekly instruction. If the cheddar is older than twenty weeks, append a move to cold storage instruction. If the cheese type is blue, and age is between four and eight weeks, append a pierce with needles instruction to allow air flow. If the type is blue and humidity is above ninety-five percent, append a reduce humidity instruction. If the cheese type is gouda, and the mold presence flag is true, append a wash with brine instruction. If the cheese type is parmesan and age is greater than one hundred weeks, append a brush rind instruction. For any cheese type, if the age exceeds fifty-two weeks and mold is present, append a discard instruction, clearing all other previous instructions. Return the list of prescribed instructions.

title: Plant Growth Regulator
spec: Write a function `regulate(plant)` that determines the nutrient and light adjustments for a greenhouse plant. The input is a list containing the plant species, growth stage, soil moisture percentage, and leaf color. If the species is tomato and the growth stage is flowering, apply a high potassium feed. If the species is lettuce and the growth stage is vegetative, apply a high nitrogen feed. If the soil moisture is below thirty percent, append a turn on irrigation command. If the soil moisture is above eighty percent, append a turn on ventilation command to dry the soil. If the leaf color is yellow and the soil moisture is normal, append an apply magnesium command. If the leaf color is purple, append an apply phosphorus command. If the growth stage is fruiting, regardless of species, reduce the lighting duration by two hours. Return a list of all determined commands and feed types.

title: Triathlon Wave Assigner
spec: Write a module to group triathlon participants into starting waves. The entry function `assign(athletes)` takes a list of tuples containing age, gender, and swim time in minutes. If gender is male and age under thirty, assign to wave one if swim time is under thirty minutes. If male and age thirty to fifty, assign to wave two if swim time is under thirty five minutes. If male and age over fifty, assign to wave three. If gender is female and age under thirty, assign to wave four if swim time is under thirty two minutes. If female and age thirty to fifty, assign to wave five. If female and age over fifty, assign to wave six. If swim time is over sixty minutes regardless of age or gender, assign to the final wave. Otherwise assign to the open wave. Return a list of wave assignment strings. Example: `[(25, "male", 28)]` returns `["wave one"]`.

title: Dim Sum Cart Pricer
spec: Calculate the bill for a dim sum meal. The entry function `tally(stamps, day)` takes a list of strings representing stamp sizes and a string for the day of the week. Small stamps are three. Medium stamps are four. Large stamps are five. Special stamps are seven. If the day is tuesday or wednesday, subtract one from every large stamp. If the day is sunday, add one to every stamp. If the day is friday and the stamp is special, add two to its price. If the total number of stamps is over twelve, apply a ten percent discount to the final total. If the list contains more than five special stamps, add a mandatory gratuity of five. If the customer has exactly zero stamps, return zero early. If the total before discount is over fifty, subtract five. If the final total is less than zero, return zero. Return the final price as a float. Example: `(["small", "large", "special"], "monday")` returns `15.0`.

title: Tornado Warning Issuer
spec: Generate automated alerts based on radar storm signatures. The entry function `warn(readings)` takes a list of tuples containing rotation speed, a boolean for funnel visible, and a string for radar echo type. If rotation speed exceeds one hundred and funnel visible is true, issue a tornado emergency. If rotation speed exceeds one hundred and funnel visible is false, issue a tornado warning. If radar echo is debris ball regardless of rotation, issue a catastrophic tornado emergency. If rotation speed is between sixty and one hundred and radar echo is hook, issue a tornado warning. If rotation speed is between sixty and one hundred and radar echo is bow, issue a severe thunderstorm warning. If rotation speed is between twenty and sixty and radar echo is hook, issue a severe weather statement. If rotation speed is under sixty and funnel visible is true, issue a spotter investigation request. If radar echo is clear and rotation speed is under twenty, issue an all clear. Otherwise issue a weather watch. Return a list of alert strings. Example: `[(120, True, "hook")]` returns `["tornado emergency"]`.

title: Safari Park Zone Router
spec: Assign incoming animals to the correct park enclosures based on their traits. The entry function `route(animals)` takes a list of tuples containing species, weight in kilos, and an aggression level string. If aggression is high and weight exceeds two hundred, route to the heavy containment zone. If aggression is high and weight is under two hundred, route to the medium carnivore enclosure. If aggression is low and weight exceeds five hundred, route to the open savanna drive. If species is primate regardless of aggression, route to the monkey jungle island. If species is reptile and weight exceeds one hundred, route to the crocodile swamp. If aggression is zero and weight is under fifty, route to the pedestrian viewing area. If species is avian and aggression is high, route to the reinforced aviary. If species is avian and aggression is low, route to the free flight dome. Otherwise route to the holding pens. Return a list of zone strings. Example: `[("lion", 250, "high")]` returns `["heavy containment zone"]`.

title: Billiards Break Evaluator
spec: Evaluate the opening break shot in a game of eight ball pool. The entry function `evaluate(breaks)` takes a list of tuples containing balls pocketed, a boolean for cue pocketed, a boolean for eight pocketed, and a boolean for scratch. If eight pocketed is true and cue pocketed is false and scratch is false, return instant win. If eight pocketed is true and cue pocketed is true, return instant loss. If eight pocketed is true and scratch is true, return instant loss. If balls pocketed is zero and scratch is false, return legal break but turn passes. If balls pocketed is greater than zero and cue pocketed is false and scratch is false, return successful break. If scratch is true and eight pocketed is false, return foul and opponent gets ball in hand. If cue pocketed is true and eight pocketed is false, return foul and opponent gets ball in hand. If balls pocketed is greater than three and no foul occurred, return excellent break. Otherwise return standard break. Return a list of outcome strings. Example: `[(4, False, False, False)]` returns `["excellent break"]`.

title: Mountaineering Pack Loadout
spec: Determine the necessary gear for an alpine expedition. The entry function `loadout(expeditions)` takes a list of tuples containing season, altitude in meters, duration in days, and a boolean for technical climbing. If season is winter and altitude is above four thousand, pack a negative forty sleeping bag and four season tent. If season is winter and altitude is below four thousand, pack a negative twenty sleeping bag. If season is summer and technical is true, pack rock shoes and a light rack. If duration is greater than five days and altitude is above three thousand, pack a heavy water melt system and extra fuel. If technical is true and season is winter, pack ice axes and crampons. If altitude is above six thousand, pack supplemental oxygen regardless of season. If season is spring and altitude is below two thousand, pack a waterproof shell and gaiters. If duration is under two days and technical is false, pack a fast and light daypack. Otherwise pack a standard trekking bag. Return a list of gear strings. Example: `[("winter", 5000, 10, True)]` returns `["negative forty sleeping bag and four season tent"]`.

title: Historical Manuscript Authenticator
spec: Evaluate the authenticity of antique documents. The entry function `authenticate(documents)` takes a list of tuples containing ink type, paper material, language, and century of origin. If century is before ten and paper material is parchment, authenticity is highly probable. If century is before fifteen and paper material is wood pulp, mark as obvious forgery. If ink type is iron gall and century is between ten and eighteen, mark as consistent with period. If language is middle english and century is after eighteen, mark as suspected revival text. If ink type is synthetic and century is before nineteen, mark as obvious forgery. If language is unknown and century is before five, mark as requiring translation specialist. If paper material is vellum and language is latin, mark as needing microscopic analysis. If century is twenty and ink type is iron gall, mark as unusual combination. Otherwise mark as standard review needed. Return a list of status strings. Example: `[("synthetic", "parchment", "latin", 12)]` returns `["obvious forgery"]`.

title: Archaeological Artifact Sorter
spec: Categorize unearthed historical items based on their properties and context. The entry function `sort(artifacts)` takes a list of tuples containing material, burial depth in meters, and region found. If depth is below five meters and material is stone, sort into paleolithic bin. If depth is between two and five meters and material is bronze, sort into bronze age bin. If depth is between one and two meters and region is mediterranean, sort into classical antiquity bin. If depth is less than one meter and region is mediterranean, sort into medieval bin. If material is ceramic and depth is below four meters, sort into ancient pottery bin. If material is iron and depth is below three meters, sort into early iron age bin. If depth is less than half a meter and material is glass, sort into modern debris bin. If material is gold and depth is below two meters, sort into high security vault. Otherwise sort into general processing bin. Return a list of bin strings. Example: `[("stone", 6, "europe")]` returns `["paleolithic bin"]`.

title: Acapella Pitch Grader
spec: Assign ratings to vocal performances based on musical criteria. The entry function `grade(vocals)` takes a list of tuples containing pitch accuracy score, vibrato control string, rhythm score, and vocal style. If pitch accuracy is above ninety five and vibrato control is excellent, award platinum rating. If pitch accuracy is above eighty five and vibrato control is good, award gold rating. If pitch accuracy is above ninety and style is beatbox, award vocal percussionist medal. If rhythm is below fifty and pitch accuracy is below fifty, award needs practice. If style is bass and pitch accuracy is above eighty, award solid foundation rating. If style is soprano and pitch accuracy is below seventy, award breath support practice. If pitch accuracy is perfect one hundred, award flawless intonation regardless of rhythm. If rhythm is perfect one hundred, award metronome medal. Otherwise award average performer rating. Return a list of rating strings. Example: `[(96, "excellent", 80, "tenor")]` returns `["platinum rating"]`.

title: Microscope Lens Selector
spec: Choose the correct objective lens and filter based on biological sample properties. The entry function `select(samples)` takes a list of tuples containing sample type, staining method, and desired magnification. If sample type is bacteria and desired magnification is one thousand, select the oil immersion objective lens. If sample type is bacteria and desired magnification is four hundred, select the high power dry lens. If sample type is tissue slice and staining is fluorescent, select the ultraviolet filter block and low power lens. If sample type is living cells and staining is none, select the phase contrast lens. If desired magnification is forty and sample type is insect, select the stereomicroscope macro lens. If sample type is crystal and staining is polarized, select the polarization filter lens. If staining is darkfield and desired magnification is over two hundred, select the specialized darkfield condenser lens. If sample type is blood smear, always select the standard high power lens. Otherwise select the general ten times objective lens. Return a list of lens strings. Example: `[("bacteria", "none", 1000)]` returns `["oil immersion objective lens"]`.

title: Kiln Temperature Controller
spec: Generate heating schedules for firing ceramic wares. The entry function `control(batches)` takes a list of tuples containing clay type, glaze thickness, and piece size. If clay type is porcelain and glaze thickness is heavy, set peak to cone ten with a four hour hold. If clay type is porcelain and glaze thickness is light, set peak to cone ten normal cycle. If clay type is wild clay and glaze thickness is heavy, set peak to cone eight with a drop and hold. If clay type is stoneware and piece size is massive, set peak to cone six with a slow preheat. If clay type is stoneware and piece size is small, set peak to cone six normal cycle. If clay type is earthenware and glaze thickness is heavy, set peak to cone zero four with a slow climb. If clay type is earthenware and glaze thickness is light, set peak to cone zero four normal cycle. If piece size is massive regardless of clay, add a twelve hour candling period at the start. If glaze thickness is none, skip the final temperature hold entirely. Return a list of instruction strings. Example: `[("porcelain", "heavy", "small")]` returns `["cone ten with a four hour hold"]`.

title: Orchid Cultivation Guide
spec: Provide care instructions for different types of greenhouse orchids. The entry function `guide(orchids)` takes a list of tuples containing genus, leaf color, root health, and humidity percentage. If genus is phalaenopsis and leaf color is dark green, increase light exposure immediately. If genus is phalaenopsis and root health is brown, stop watering and apply fungicide. If genus is cattleya and humidity is below forty, add a humidifier and mist daily. If genus is cattleya and leaf color is yellow, reduce light exposure. If genus is vanda and root health is silvery, water heavily until roots turn green. If genus is paphiopedilum and leaf color is pale, apply a weak magnesium fertilizer. If genus is dendrobium and humidity is above eighty, increase air circulation to prevent rot. If root health is mushy regardless of genus, unpot and trim dead roots immediately. Otherwise maintain current care routine. Return a list of care strings. Example: `[("phalaenopsis", "dark green", "green", 50)]` returns `["increase light exposure immediately"]`.

title: Perfume Blending Advisor
spec: Suggest essential oil combinations based on desired fragrance profiles. The entry function `blend(profiles)` takes a list of tuples containing dominant note, intensity, and target occasion. If dominant note is floral and target occasion is daytime, select rose and jasmine with light carrier oil. If dominant note is floral and target occasion is evening, select tuberose and ylang ylang with heavy carrier oil. If dominant note is woody and intensity is strong, select sandalwood and cedar with a touch of patchouli. If dominant note is woody and target occasion is daytime, select vetiver and bergamot. If dominant note is oriental and target occasion is evening, select vanilla and amber. If dominant note is aquatic and target occasion is daytime, select sea salt and melon. If dominant note is citrus and target occasion is daytime, select lemon and grapefruit. If intensity is very weak, select a musk base to fix the scent without overpowering. Otherwise select a balanced blend of lavender and oakmoss. Return a list of blend strings. Example: `[("floral", "strong", "evening")]` returns `["tuberose and ylang ylang with heavy carrier oil"]`.

title: Apiary Colony Inspector
spec: Recommend interventions for beekeepers based on hive inspection data. The entry function `inspect(colonies)` takes a list of tuples containing mite count, brood pattern string, honey stores string, and weather condition. If mite count is over ten and brood pattern is spotty, recommend immediate varroa treatment. If mite count is over ten and brood pattern is solid, recommend varroa monitoring and gentle treatment. If brood pattern is spotty and honey stores are low, recommend feeding pollen substitute and sugar syrup. If brood pattern is solid and honey stores are high, recommend adding a honey super box. If honey stores are very low and weather is cold, recommend emergency winter fondant feeding. If weather is stormy and honey stores are high, recommend adding a heavy roof weight. If mite count is zero and brood pattern is solid, recommend no action needed. If brood pattern is completely absent, recommend requeening the hive immediately. Otherwise recommend standard weekly inspection. Return a list of recommendation strings. Example: `[(12, "spotty", "high", "warm")]` returns `["immediate varroa treatment"]`.

title: Martial Arts Belt Grader
spec: Evaluate student eligibility for rank promotion. The entry function `grade(candidates)` takes a list of tuples containing attendance count, kata score, sparring score, and current rank string. If current rank is white and attendance is over twenty and kata score is over fifty, promote to yellow belt. If current rank is yellow and kata score is over seventy and sparring score is over fifty, promote to orange belt. If current rank is orange and attendance is over forty and sparring score is over seventy, promote to green belt. If current rank is green and kata score is over eighty and sparring score is over eighty, promote to blue belt. If current rank is brown and attendance is over one hundred and kata score is over ninety and sparring score is over ninety, promote to black belt. If current rank is black and attendance is over two hundred, promote to second degree black belt. If attendance is under ten, fail due to absence. If kata score is under forty, fail due to poor technique. Otherwise return retest required. Return a list of promotion strings. Example: `[(25, 60, 50, "white")]` returns `["promote to yellow belt"]`.

title: Snowboard Stance Calculator
spec: Determine the optimal binding setup for a snowboarder. The entry function `calculate(riders)` takes a list of tuples containing height in centimeters, riding style, boot size, and experience level. If riding style is freestyle and experience is beginner, set stance width to fifty centimeters and angles to zero. If riding style is freestyle and experience is advanced, set stance width to fifty five centimeters and angles to duck stance. If riding style is freeride and height is over one hundred eighty, set stance width to sixty centimeters and angles to positive directional. If riding style is freeride and height is under one hundred eighty, set stance width to fifty two centimeters. If riding style is alpine and experience is advanced, set stance to forward racing angles. If boot size is over eleven, add wide board requirement and increase angles by three degrees. If boot size is under seven, add narrow board requirement. If experience is expert regardless of style, suggest custom micro adjustments. Otherwise set stance to standard fifty centimeters and mild positive angles. Return a list of stance strings. Example: `[(170, "freestyle", 9, "beginner")]` returns `["fifty centimeters and angles to zero"]`.

title: Fermentation Batch Validator
spec: Monitor and direct the progress of fermenting beverages. The entry function `validate(batches)` takes a list of tuples containing ph level, temperature in celsius, gravity string, and days active. If ph level is below four and gravity is stable, mark batch as complete and ready for bottling. If ph level is above five and days active is over seven, mark batch as stalled and add yeast nutrient. If temperature is over thirty five and days active is over three, mark batch as heat damaged and discard. If temperature is over thirty and ph level is below four, mark batch as at risk of fusel alcohols and chill immediately. If temperature is under fifteen and gravity is dropping slowly, mark batch as slow ferment and warm the vessel. If days active is over fourteen and gravity is not stable, mark batch as struggling and rouse the yeast. If ph level is below three point two, mark batch as overly acidic and consider blending. If gravity is extremely high and days active is zero, mark batch as ready to pitch yeast. Otherwise mark batch as actively fermenting. Return a list of status strings. Example: `[(3.8, 20, "stable", 10)]` returns `["ready for bottling"]`.

title: Excavator Attachment Selector
spec: Recommend the correct heavy machinery attachment for earthmoving tasks. The entry function `select(jobs)` takes a list of tuples containing soil type, digging depth, a boolean for rocks present, and a boolean for precision needed. If soil type is clay and rocks present is true, select the heavy duty rock bucket with teeth. If soil type is clay and rocks present is false, select the standard digging bucket. If soil type is sand and digging depth is shallow, select the wide grading bucket. If soil type is sand and precision needed is true, select the tilt bucket. If soil type is gravel and digging depth is shallow, select the skeleton sifting bucket. If rocks present is true and precision needed is true, select the hydraulic thumb attachment. If digging depth is very deep and soil type is loose, select the long reach boom extension. If soil type is frozen, select the hydraulic breaker attachment immediately. Otherwise select the general purpose bucket. Return a list of attachment strings. Example: `[("clay", "deep", True, False)]` returns `["heavy duty rock bucket with teeth"]`.

title: Brewery Mash Temperature Director
spec: Provide step mashing instructions for brewing beer. The entry function `direct(mashes)` takes a list of tuples containing beer style, malt type, target body, and current temperature. If beer style is stout and target body is full, raise temperature to sixty eight degrees for alpha amylase extraction. If beer style is pilsner and target body is light, lower temperature to sixty four degrees for beta amylase extraction. If beer style is sour and target body is light, lower temperature to sixty degrees for a prolonged rest. If malt type is wheat and current temp is under fifty, perform a ferulic acid rest at forty five degrees. If malt type is unmalted adjunct and current temp is under eighty, perform a cereal mash at eighty five degrees. If target body is medium and current temp is sixty six, maintain current temperature for saccharification. If beer style is hazy ipa and malt type is oats, raise temperature to sixty nine degrees. If current temp is over seventy five, initiate mash out to denature enzymes. Otherwise maintain sixty five degrees. Return a list of instruction strings. Example: `[("stout", "pale", "full", 60)]` returns `["raise temperature to sixty eight degrees"]`.

title: Satellite Dish Band Allocator
spec: Assign transmission frequencies to communications dishes based on environmental factors. The entry function `allocate(links)` takes a list of tuples containing rain fade risk, bandwidth needed, dish size, and priority level. If rain fade risk is high and bandwidth needed is low, allocate the c band frequency. If rain fade risk is high and bandwidth needed is high, allocate the ku band with maximum error correction. If rain fade risk is low and bandwidth needed is extremely high, allocate the ka band frequency. If dish size is small and priority is high, allocate the ku band directed beam. If priority is emergency response and rain fade risk is high, allocate the l band frequency. If priority is critical military, allocate the x band frequency regardless of weather. If bandwidth needed is low and dish size is very large, allocate the ultra high frequency fallback band. If priority is low and rain fade risk is extreme, suspend the link transmission. Otherwise allocate standard ku band. Return a list of band strings. Example: `[("high", "low", "large", "normal")]` returns `["c band frequency"]`.

title: Opera Audition Caster
spec: Cast vocalists into classical roles based on their range and vocal qualities. The entry function `cast(singers)` takes a list of tuples containing lowest note, highest note, timbre, and agility level. If lowest note is E two and highest note is E four and timbre is dark, cast as dramatic bass. If lowest note is C three and highest note is G four and timbre is bright, cast as lyric tenor. If lowest note is F three and highest note is D five and timbre is dark, cast as dramatic contralto. If lowest note is G three and highest note is B five and timbre is dark, cast as dramatic soprano. If lowest note is C four and highest note is C six and agility is high, cast as coloratura soprano. If highest note is above C six and agility is exceptional, cast as Queen of the Night role. If lowest note is below C two, cast as basso profondo specialist. If lowest note is A two and highest note is A four, cast as lyric baritone. Otherwise cast as ensemble chorus member. Return a list of role strings. Example: `[("C4", "C6", "bright", "high")]` returns `["coloratura soprano"]`.

title: Diamond Clarity Grader
spec: Evaluate gemstones to assign them an industry standard clarity grade. The entry function `grade(diamonds)` takes a list of tuples containing inclusion size, inclusion count, inclusion location, and a boolean for magnification visible. If inclusion size is none and magnification visible is false, grade as flawless. If inclusion size is tiny and inclusion count is one and magnification visible is true at ten times, grade as very very slightly included. If inclusion size is small and inclusion location is center, grade as slightly included type two. If inclusion size is small and inclusion location is edge, grade as slightly included type one. If inclusion count is over five and magnification visible is true at naked eye, grade as included type three. If inclusion size is large and inclusion location is center, grade as included type two regardless of count. If inclusion size is massive and inclusion location is center, grade as industrial quality diamond. If inclusion size is microscopic and count is under three, grade as very slightly included. Otherwise grade as included type one. Return a list of grade strings. Example: `[("none", 0, "edge", False)]` returns `["flawless"]`.

title: Pyrotechnic Launch Sequencer
spec: Control the timing and safety constraints of a fireworks display. The entry function `sequence(fireworks)` takes a list of tuples containing shell size in inches, effect type, wind speed, and audience distance. If shell size is over eight inches and wind speed is over fifteen, abort the launch of this shell. If shell size is over eight inches and audience distance is under five hundred, abort due to proximity limits. If effect type is willow and wind speed is over ten, adjust launch angle by five degrees downwind. If effect type is strobe and wind speed is over twenty, cancel due to visibility loss. If effect type is peony and shell size is under four inches, launch immediately with zero delay. If effect type is chrysanthemum and shell size is six inches, set fuse delay to two seconds. If effect type is grand finale and audience distance is over one thousand, chain all remaining shells to launch simultaneously. If wind speed is under five and shell size is large, launch perfectly vertical. Otherwise set fuse delay to one second and launch vertical. Return a list of command strings. Example: `[(10, "willow", 20, 800)]` returns `["abort the launch of this shell"]`.

title: Vineyard Soil Amendment Guide
spec: Suggest soil treatments to viticulturists based on soil tests and planted varietals. The entry function `amend(samples)` takes a list of tuples containing nitrogen level, phosphorus level, potassium level, and grape variety. If nitrogen level is low and grape variety is cabernet, apply heavy organic compost. If nitrogen level is low and grape variety is chardonnay, apply a light foliar spray to avoid excessive vigor. If phosphorus level is low and grape variety is pinot noir, apply bone meal directly to the root zone. If potassium level is low and grape variety is merlot, apply kelp extract to boost fruit development. If all three levels are high, apply zero amendments and increase cover crop planting. If grape variety is sauvignon blanc and nitrogen level is medium, apply fish emulsion. If phosphorus level is high and potassium level is low, apply greensand. If grape variety is syrah and nitrogen level is low, apply a balanced synthetic mix. Otherwise apply general purpose mulch. Return a list of amendment strings. Example: `[("low", "adequate", "adequate", "cabernet")]` returns `["heavy organic compost"]`.

title: Kombucha Flavoring Director
spec: Recommend secondary fermentation additions for batches of fermented tea. The entry function `flavor(batches)` takes a list of tuples containing base tea, acidity level, sweetness level, and target profile. If base tea is black and acidity level is high, add ginger and turmeric to balance the bite. If base tea is black and sweetness level is high, add tart cherry juice. If base tea is green and target profile is floral, add lavender and chamomile. If base tea is green and acidity level is low, add lemon juice and hibiscus. If base tea is white and target profile is delicate, add peach puree and a sprig of mint. If base tea is pu erh and target profile is earthy, add beetroot and ginger juice. If base tea is oolong and sweetness level is low, add mango and extra cane sugar. If acidity level is extremely high regardless of tea, dilute with water and add baking soda. Otherwise add mixed berries for a standard flavor. Return a list of ingredient strings. Example: `[("black", "high", "low", "spicy")]` returns `["ginger and turmeric"]`.

title: Emergency Room Triage
spec: Write a function `triage(patients)` that determines the priority level from one to five for incoming hospital cases. Each patient provides their age, temperature, heart rate, and pain level on a ten point scale. If the heart rate is over one hundred twenty or under fifty, assign priority one immediately. If the pain level is ten, assign priority two, but if the temperature is over one hundred three, assign priority two unless the patient is under three or over sixty five years old, which elevates it to priority one. If the pain level is above seven, assign priority three. If the temperature is below ninety five, assign priority one, otherwise default to priority four unless the age is under twelve, which makes it priority three. Finally, if the temperature is normal between ninety seven and ninety nine and pain is below three, assign priority five. Return a list of the assigned priority levels in the same order as the inputs. Example: given a fifty year old with normal temp, eighty heart rate, and pain two, return five.

title: Real Estate Zoning Checker
spec: Write a function `zone(properties)` that validates building proposals based on lot size, building height, usage type, and front setback distance. For a residential usage, the lot size must be over five thousand square feet and height under forty feet. For a commercial usage, the lot size must be over ten thousand and height under one hundred. For an industrial usage, the lot size must be over twenty thousand. The setback must be at least ten feet for residential and twenty feet for commercial, but if a residential building height is over thirty feet, the setback must be at least fifteen feet. If a property is industrial, it must have a setback of at least thirty feet and cannot be over fifty feet high. Reject any proposal that fails its specific criteria or has an unknown usage type. Return a list of accepted or rejected statuses for each proposal. Example: a commercial building with lot size twelve thousand, height eighty, and setback twenty five would return accepted.

title: Cargo Ship Load Balancer
spec: Implement a function `balance(containers)` that assigns shipping containers to the port side, starboard side, or center of a vessel to maintain stability. Iterate through the containers evaluating their weight and type. Heavy containers weighing over ten thousand pounds must go to the center. Hazardous materials go to the port side if their weight is under five thousand pounds, otherwise they must go to the center. Refrigerated containers strictly go to the starboard side. For standard containers, compare the current total weight assigned to the port and starboard sides and assign the container to whichever side is currently lighter. If the weights are exactly equal, place standard containers on the port side. If a container is marked as empty, always assign it to the top deck regardless of other rules. Return a list of the assigned locations for each container. Example: an empty container returns top deck, while a standard container of two thousand pounds goes port.

title: Hospital Payroll Shift Differential
spec: Create a function `payroll(shifts)` that calculates the total pay for hospital staff based on their base rate, hours worked, and shift conditions. The standard pay multiplier is one. If the shift falls on a weekend, add zero point five to the multiplier. If it is a night shift, add zero point two. However, if it is a holiday and a night shift, add one point zero total instead of the normal night shift bonus. If the shift exceeds eight hours, the overtime hours beyond eight receive a flat one point five multiplier regardless of other bonuses. If the shift is a double shift over sixteen hours, add a fixed fifty dollar hazard bonus. If the employee is marked as on call but not called in, their multiplier for the entire shift is zero point two and no other bonuses apply. If the employee is a trainee, their final pay is strictly capped at one hundred dollars. Return a list of total calculated pay amounts for each shift. Example: an eight hour weekend night shift at ten dollars an hour uses a one point seven multiplier, returning one hundred thirty six dollars.

title: Forest Fire Risk Evaluator
spec: Develop a function `risk(regions)` that assesses the wildfire danger level for different areas based on temperature, humidity, wind speed, and days since last rainfall. Start by assigning a low risk if rain has fallen within the last two days. If the temperature is over ninety degrees and wind speed is over twenty miles per hour, the risk becomes extreme. If humidity is under twenty percent and the temperature is over eighty, set the risk to high. If it has been more than fourteen days since the last rain and the temperature is over seventy, the risk is also high. Additionally, if the wind speed exceeds thirty miles per hour, elevate the current risk level by one tier from low to moderate, moderate to high, or high to extreme. If the temperature is below freezing, the risk is always none regardless of other factors. Return a list of the final risk levels for each region. Example: eighty five degrees, fifteen percent humidity, and ten days since rain returns high.

title: Cloud Server Auto Scaler
spec: Write a function `scale(metrics)` that decides whether to add, remove, or keep cloud servers active based on minute by minute usage data. For each minute, evaluate the cpu percentage, memory percentage, and active connections. If the cpu is over eighty percent or memory is over ninety percent, recommend adding two servers. If the cpu is over seventy percent and connections are over one thousand, recommend adding one server. If the cpu is under twenty percent, memory is under thirty percent, and connections are under one hundred, recommend removing one server. If the cpu remains under ten percent for three consecutive checks, recommend removing two servers. If connections drop to exactly zero, recommend shutting down all servers except one. Otherwise, recommend keeping the current count. Return a list of the recommended actions for each minute. Example: ninety five percent memory recommends adding two servers.

title: Earthquake Damage Estimator
spec: Create a function `estimate(quakes)` that predicts structural damage levels based on earthquake magnitude, depth in miles, and primary building material. Base damage is none for magnitudes under four. Magnitudes over seven cause severe damage, unless the depth is over one hundred miles, which reduces it to moderate. Magnitudes between five and seven cause moderate damage. For unreinforced masonry structures, increase the damage by one level from none to moderate, or moderate to severe. For wood frame structures, decrease the damage by one level if the magnitude is under six. If the depth is under ten miles and the magnitude is over six, increase the damage by one level for any material. A magnitude exactly equal to nine always results in catastrophic damage. Return a list of the predicted final damage levels. Example: magnitude six point five at five miles depth for wood frame returns severe.

title: Automated Radio Scheduler
spec: Implement a function `schedule(tracks)` that builds a sixty minute radio broadcast playlist from a sequence of available songs and segments. Iterate through the tracks, keeping a running total of the duration. You cannot play two rock songs consecutively. You must insert an advertisement if fifteen minutes have passed since the last ad. If a track is a pop song, it can follow any genre without restriction. If a track is classical, it can only be played if the current total time is under thirty minutes. If adding a track pushes the total duration strictly over sixty minutes, skip it. If a track is an interview, it must not be the first or last item in the scheduled playlist. Skip any track that has explicit lyrics if the broadcast is marked daytime. Return a list of the selected track titles in order. Example: a ten minute rock song and a five minute pop song are both added if they fit the time limit.

title: Blood Pressure Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(readings)` that categorizes systolic and diastolic blood pressure pairs. A normal reading is systolic under one hundred twenty and diastolic under eighty. An elevated reading is systolic between one hundred twenty and one hundred twenty nine, and diastolic under eighty. Hypertension stage one is defined as systolic between one hundred thirty and one hundred thirty nine, or diastolic between eighty and eighty nine. Hypertension stage two occurs if systolic is one hundred forty or higher, or diastolic is ninety or higher. A hypertensive crisis is triggered if systolic is over one hundred eighty or diastolic is over one hundred twenty. If a crisis is detected, skip all other category checks immediately. If the systolic is lower than ninety and diastolic lower than sixty, categorize as hypotension. Return a list of the highest severity categories matched for each pair. Example: one hundred twenty five over seventy five returns elevated.

title: Wildlife Collar Anomaly Detector
spec: Develop a function `monitor(data)` that flags abnormal animal behavior from daily tracking collar records containing distance traveled, body temperature, and average heart rate. A normal daily distance is between two and ten miles, and normal temperature is between ninety eight and one hundred two degrees. Flag an anomaly if the distance is under one mile, unless the temperature is below thirty degrees indicating hibernation. Flag an anomaly if the temperature exceeds one hundred four degrees, suggesting fever. Flag an anomaly if the heart rate is over one hundred fifty beats per minute while the distance is under one mile, indicating stress. Flag an anomaly if the distance is over twenty miles, suggesting the animal is fleeing. If the heart rate drops below forty, flag it as critical condition. Return a list of the specific anomaly reasons or a normal status for each daily record. Example: distance zero and temperature twenty returns normal due to hibernation.

title: E-Sport Bracket Seeding
spec: Create a function `seed(teams)` that assigns teams from various regions to four distinct tournament groups to prevent early regional knockouts. Loop through the teams sorted by their global rank. Assign each team to group one, two, three, or four based on which group currently contains the fewest teams. If multiple groups are tied in size, assign the team to the group that has the fewest teams from the incoming team's specific region. If there is still a tie, assign the team to the group with the lowest numerical identifier. If a group already contains two teams from the same region, skip that group entirely unless all groups already have two teams from that region. If a team is marked as a wild card, they must be assigned to group four regardless of size, unless group four is strictly full at four teams. Return a list containing four lists of assigned teams. Example: the top ranked team naturally goes to group one if all are empty.

title: Automated Warehouse Robot Routing
spec: Implement a function `route(tasks)` that assigns item retrieval jobs to different warehouse robot zones based on item weight, fragility, and priority. Heavy items over fifty pounds must be sent to the heavy zone, unless they are also fragile, in which case they require manual handling. Items marked high priority must go to the express zone if they weigh under ten pounds. Fragile items weighing under fifty pounds go to the careful zone. Normal items that do not meet these criteria go to the standard zone. If the standard zone has more than ten items assigned to it, route any subsequent standard items to the bulk overflow zone. If an item is hazardous, immediately route it to the isolation zone and ignore all other rules. Return a list of the assigned zones for each task in the same order. Example: a five pound high priority item returns express zone.

title: Personal Tax Deduction Checker
spec: Write a function `deduct(expenses)` that evaluates personal expenditures for tax deductibility based on the expense type, amount, and total annual income. Loop over the submitted expenses. Medical expenses are deductible only for the amount that exceeds seven percent of the total income. Education expenses are fully deductible up to four thousand dollars, but only if the total income is under eighty thousand dollars; otherwise they are not deductible at all. Home office expenses are deductible only if the person is self employed and the office area is strictly over ten percent of the total home square footage. Charity donations are fully deductible up to a maximum of sixty percent of the total income. Entertainment expenses are never deductible. Return a list of the calculated deductible amounts for each expense. Example: a one thousand dollar charity donation with fifty thousand income returns one thousand.

title: Train Ticket Refund Calculator
spec: Develop a function `refund(tickets)` that calculates the money to return for canceled journeys based on the ticket class and the number of days until departure. Non refundable tickets always get zero dollars back. Fully flexible tickets get one hundred percent of the base price back regardless of timing. Standard tickets get ninety percent back if canceled more than fourteen days before departure. Between seven and fourteen days inclusive, standard tickets get fifty percent back. With fewer than seven days notice, standard tickets get zero back. If any ticket includes a meal add on, the meal portion is fully refunded regardless of the days left, unless the cancellation happens under twenty four hours before departure, in which case the meal refund is also zero. Return a list of total refund amounts for each ticket. Example: a standard ticket with fifty dollars base price canceled ten days out returns twenty five dollars.

title: Agricultural Crop Rotation Advisor
spec: Create a function `rotate(fields)` that recommends the next crop to plant based on soil nitrogen levels, the previous crop, and the upcoming season. If the soil nitrogen is low, recommend planting legumes like peas or beans. If the previous crop was corn and the nitrogen is normal, recommend planting soybeans to replenish nutrients. If the upcoming season is winter, recommend planting winter wheat, unless the nitrogen is very low, in which case recommend leaving the field fallow. If the previous crop was potatoes, recommend planting corn next. If the nitrogen is high, recommend planting heavy feeders like tomatoes or cabbage. If the field has a history of blight and the season is summer, recommend a resistant crop like barley and ignore the previous crop rules. Return a list of the recommendations for each field. Example: low nitrogen in spring returns legumes.

title: Custom URL Protocol Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(urls)` that extracts components from custom uniform resource locators without using external networking libraries. Loop over the provided string addresses. First, split the string by the colon slash slash separator; if it is missing, mark the entire address as invalid. The portion before the separator is the scheme. If the scheme is secure, the default port is four four three. If the scheme is file, the default port is zero. Find the very first slash in the remaining portion to separate the host from the path. If there is a question mark in the path, split it into the path and the query string. If a hash symbol is present, split off the fragment identifier. If the host contains an at symbol, separate the username from the host. Return a list of the extracted host names, or invalid strings, for each address. Example: secure colon slash slash example dot com slash home returns example dot com.

title: Automated Bartender Mixer
spec: Implement a function `mix(orders)` that checks available ingredients to fulfill cocktail requests and outputs the preparation steps. For a martini, you need gin and vermouth; if out of gin, substitute vodka if available, but if neither is available, reject the order. For a margarita, you need tequila, lime, and triple sec; if there is no triple sec, substitute agave syrup. For an old fashioned, you need bourbon and bitters. If the drink contains any citrus juice, add a shake step, otherwise add a stir step. Finally, garnish with an olive for a martini, a lime wedge for a margarita, and a cherry for an old fashioned. If the order is a mocktail, skip the alcohol checks and use soda water instead. Return a list of step sequences or a rejected status for each order. Example: a margarita with all ingredients returns shake tequila lime triple sec then garnish with lime.

title: Video Game Character State Machine
spec: Develop a function `update(inputs)` that determines a video game character's movement state based on their current state and a sequence of player button presses. Start in the idle state. If the state is idle and the input is forward, change to the walking state. If walking and the input is sprint, change to running. If the character is in the air, all horizontal inputs are ignored until a landing input is received. If the input is jump and the state is not already in the air, change to the in air state. If the input is crouch, change to crouching only if the current state is idle or walking. If crouching and the input is jump, stand up and change to idle instead of going into the air. If running and the input is crouch, change to the sliding state. Return a list of the chronological states produced by the inputs. Example: idle then forward then jump returns walking then in air.

title: Automated CV Screener
spec: Create a function `screen(resumes)` that scores job applicants based on their education level, years of experience, and keyword matches. A bachelor degree adds ten points, a master degree adds twenty points, and a doctorate adds thirty points. Each year of professional experience adds five points, up to a strict maximum of fifty points. However, if the candidate has over ten years of experience, skip the education points entirely as experience takes precedence. If the keyword python or the keyword java is present in the skills section, add fifteen points. If the keyword leadership is present, add ten points. If the candidate requires visa sponsorship, subtract twenty points. If the final score is over seventy, mark the status as interview, otherwise mark as reject. Return a list of the final statuses for all candidates. Example: five years experience, bachelor degree, and python returns interview.

title: Boarding House Room Assignment
spec: Write a function `assign(guests)` that places incoming visitors into standard, quiet, or pet friendly wings of a lodge. Iterate over the guest profiles. If a guest brings a pet, they must be assigned to the pet friendly wing. If a guest is a smoker, assign them to the standard wing with a balcony restriction. If a guest is over sixty years old or explicitly requests quiet, assign them to the quiet wing. If the quiet wing reaches its maximum capacity of five guests, fallback to the standard wing for any subsequent quiet requests. If a guest is under eighteen years old, they must be placed in the exact same wing as their parent or guardian, bypassing their own preferences. If a guest brings a musical instrument, they cannot be placed in the quiet wing. Return a list of the final wing assignments. Example: a sixty five year old guest with no pets returns quiet wing.

title: Custom String Encryption
spec: Implement a function `encrypt(messages)` that shifts characters in a text based on their position and alphabetical type. Iterate over the messages and then over each character. If the character is an uppercase vowel, shift it forward in the alphabet by three positions. If it is an uppercase consonant, shift it backward by one position. If it is a lowercase vowel, shift it forward by five positions. If it is a lowercase consonant, shift it backward by two positions. If the character is a numerical digit, replace it with nine minus that digit. If it is a space, leave it unmodified as a space. If it is a punctuation mark, swap it with the immediate next character in the string, assuming the next character is also a punctuation mark. Return a list of the fully encrypted message strings. Example: an uppercase A becomes an uppercase D, and a zero becomes a nine.

title: Theme Park Crowd Distributor
spec: Develop a function `distribute(groups)` that directs incoming park guests to different themed lands to dynamically balance crowd levels. Look at each guest group. If the group has children under ten, direct them to fantasy land, unless fantasy land is currently at over eighty percent capacity, in which case direct them to toon town. If there are teenagers in the group, direct them to thrill land. If the group average age is over sixty, direct them to history land. Regardless of demographics, if any land reaches ninety percent capacity, temporarily route all subsequent groups to whichever land has the absolute lowest current capacity until the congested land drops below ninety percent. If a group has a VIP pass, they always go to their requested land regardless of capacity. Return a list of the directed lands for each group. Example: a group with a five year old goes to fantasy land.

title: Musical Chord Identifier
spec: Create a function `identify(chords)` that names musical chords based on the number of semitones between consecutive notes. Calculate the intervals from the first to second note, and second to third note. An interval of four semitones followed by three semitones is a major chord. Three followed by four is a minor chord. Three followed by three is a diminished chord. Four followed by four is an augmented chord. If a fourth note is present and the interval from the root to the fourth note is ten semitones, append dominant seventh to the name. If the interval is eleven semitones, append major seventh. If the interval is nine semitones, append diminished seventh. If the base intervals do not match any standard pattern, mark the chord as unknown. Return a list of the identified chord names. Example: intervals of four then three returns major.

title: Vehicle License Plate Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(plates)` that checks if custom vehicle license plates meet regional syntax rules. Each plate string must be strictly between six and eight characters long. The first two characters must always be alphabetical letters. If the third character is a numerical digit, the system classifies it as a commercial vehicle, and therefore the very last character must be a letter. If it is classified as a personal vehicle, the string must end with exactly two numerical digits. The letters O and I are strictly prohibited anywhere in the string to avoid visual confusion with zero and one. If a plate is exactly seven characters long, the middle character must be a hyphen. If any of these rules fail, mark the plate as invalid. Return a list of valid or invalid statuses for each input. Example: AB three four five six returns valid as a personal vehicle plate.

title: Automated Driving Collision Avoidance
spec: Implement a function `drive(sensors)` that determines the next maneuver for a self driving vehicle based on current speed, distance to the nearest obstacle, and the obstacle type. If the distance is under twenty meters and the speed is over thirty miles per hour, trigger the emergency brake. If the distance is under fifty meters and the obstacle is a pedestrian, also trigger the emergency brake. If the obstacle is a vehicle and the current speed is greater than the obstacle's speed, smoothly decelerate. If the obstacle is an animal, activate the horn and decelerate. If the distance is over one hundred meters, maintain the current speed. If the sensors indicate the vehicle is drifting out of the current lane, apply a steer center correction regardless of obstacles unless an emergency brake is active. Return a list of the chosen maneuvers. Example: ten meters from a wall at forty miles per hour returns emergency brake.

title: Knitting Pattern Tracker
spec: Process a string of commands to determine the final width of a knitted fabric. Write the function `knit(stitches)` taking a string of commands separated by spaces. Loop through the words, applying these rules: if knit, add one to width; if purl, add one to width and increment texture; if over, add two to width; if drop, decrease width by one; if slip, leave width unchanged; if bind, terminate the loop. If the width drops below zero, set a failure flag. If the command is completely unknown, ignore it. For example, the input string knit purl drop results in a width of one, a texture count of one, and a failure boolean of false.

title: Historical Telegraph Message Parser
spec: Evaluate a string of historical telegraph pulses and words. Write the function `telegraph(signal)` that takes a single string of words. Loop through the words: if the word is stop, insert a period into the message without charging; if urgent, capitalize the next word; if break, insert a newline; if repeat, duplicate the previous word; if unknown, append it and increment the billed word count. If the word is an empty string, skip it entirely. If the accumulated billed word count exceeds fifty, apply a bulk discount by subtracting two from the cost. If the message ends up completely empty, set the cost to zero.
